identities.essence: a² + b² = c² — the Pythagorean theorem made spatial: three squares grown from triangle sides
identities.desire: learner sees the theorem not as a formula but as an area relationship — squares fitting together
identities.critical_parameter: the right angle vertex — fixing it keeps the right angle while the learner explores leg ratios
identities.triggers: dragging any vertex — hypotenuse square resizes to match the sum of the two leg squares
identities.emerges: the theorem as a visual conservation law — the big square always equals the two small squares combined
identities.needs: [has grabbable vertex spheres [has], has formula Label3D (a²+b²≈c²) [has], missing VR angle slider]
identities.relationships: sibling to triangle; depends on understanding line length; connects to rotation via angles
identities.truth: the Pythagorean theorem is a statement about areas, not lengths — c² is literally a square

identities.essence: triangle(v0, v1, v2) — the minimal surface: 3 points that define a plane and a bounded region
identities.desire: learner feels how a surface deforms when its boundary points move — topology through touch
identities.critical_parameter: the double-sided mesh — front and back are different colors, making orientation visible
identities.triggers: dragging any vertex grab sphere — mesh rebuilds instantly to reflect new positions; area displayed on drop
identities.emerges: the area formula as something felt — move vertices apart, area grows; collapse them, area vanishes
identities.needs: [has 3 grabbable vertex spheres [has], missing area-threshold feedback or VR slider]
identities.relationships: atomic unit of all 3D meshes; logical predecessor to quad, folded_strip, animatedcubebuilder
identities.truth: every surface in 3D graphics is an agreement among three points — all meshes are triangles

identities.essence: zigzag(n_triangles, height_high, height_low) — a strip of alternating triangles forming a pleat profile
identities.desire: learner feels how a complex perimeter shape is just many small triangles sharing edges
identities.critical_parameter: grab_point_count — how many vertex handles exist along the zigzag strip perimeter
identities.triggers: dragging any grab handle — the triangle strip deforms, showing how local edits ripple through profile
identities.emerges: the strip as a minimal surface description — pleats and folds arise from alternating vertex heights
identities.needs: [has many grabbable vertex handles [has], missing global height/frequency sliders]
identities.relationships: sibling to triangle; demonstrates that profiles and extrusions are just strips of triangles
identities.truth: a complex surface profile is built from the simplest unit — a triangle — repeated with shared edges

identities.essence: trihedron — 4 vertices, 3 triangular faces and 1 quad base: the wedge as 3D primitive
identities.desire: learner holds a 3D solid, turns it in their hands, and counts faces, edges, vertices
identities.critical_parameter: button material toggle — pressing reveals the internal structure through a different material
identities.triggers: pick up → snaps to shelf; button press → alternates material showing surface vs wireframe quality
identities.emerges: the Euler relation (V-E+F=2) as something you count by holding; topology felt through handling
identities.needs: [has VR button (material toggle) [has], has shelf snap [has], missing edge/vertex count label]
identities.relationships: sibling to grab_octahedron; both teach held polyhedra with button interaction
identities.truth: a solid is defined by its topology — how faces connect — not by any particular material or color

identities.essence: tetrahedron with corners cut — each vertex replaced by a triangular face, adding 4 new faces
identities.desire: learner sees truncation as a topological operation: vertices become faces, edges become edges
identities.critical_parameter: base_color — orange pride color that signals this is a pedagogical display object

identities.needs: [missing VR controls — static display only]
identities.relationships: sibling to grab_tetrahedron and snap_tetrahedron_puzzle; shows topology via truncation
identities.truth: truncation is a functor — it transforms the vertex-edge-face structure systematically

identities.essence: trace(t) = (target.x, target.y, z_origin - speed * t) — position history as fading trail
identities.desire: Toss a pickup cube and see its trajectory recorded as a time-domain trace in space
identities.critical_parameter: time_axis_speed — controls how fast the trace extends along the Z axis
identities.triggers: continuous position sampling of target node at sample_interval creates the fading trail
identities.emerges: thrown trajectories become visible waveforms — parabolas, oscillations, chaos all recorded
identities.needs: VR pickup cube to track [has], trail rendering [has]
identities.relationships: depends on target node position sampling; contrasts with draw_dot_time_domain (cube tracking vs hand tracking); unlocks trajectory visualization
identities.truth: Every trajectory is a signal in time; recording it reveals the physics as waveform.

identities.essence: grab → step(algorithm, image, t) → drop → pause. The paper is a universal Turing surface.
identities.desire: To be held — the algorithm only runs while grabbed, making the learner's hand the clock signal
identities.critical_parameter: algorithm enum — 35 algorithms from random walks to Mandelbrot, each a different cartridge in the same machine
identities.triggers: grab → _is_walking = true → steps accumulate on texture; drop → freeze; config swap → new algorithm
identities.emerges: The paper's visual history — every step leaves a permanent mark, creating a fossil record of computation
identities.needs: VR grab [has], algorithm swap via config [has], speed control [missing]
identities.relationships: Universal substrate appearing across all sequences; each algorithm cartridge connects to its parent sequence
identities.truth: The paper does not compute — the hand that holds it does. Grab is the clock. Drop is halt.

identities.essence: vr_scene(no_headset) -> player_figure + posed_hands + environment -> headless still
identities.desire: make VR-only gestures evaluable by the chamber/DNA pattern without needing a headset
identities.critical_parameter: hand_basis (orientation math), camera angle (elevated 3/4), capture-only visual aids (kept out of production)
identities.triggers: static calls from any capture_* script; returns built nodes for further composition
identities.emerges: the auto-research-DNA pattern extends to VR-only artifacts — gestures, two-handed interactions, controller-relative behaviours

identities.essence: label.text = Engine.get_process_frames() — a live counter of rendered frames since startup
identities.desire: learner understands that VR runs as a discrete sequence of frames, not a continuous flow
identities.critical_parameter: the update rate — _process fires once per frame, so the counter increments with each render
identities.triggers: every rendered frame — the number ticks up continuously; pausing the game stops the counter
identities.emerges: the frame as the fundamental unit of VR time — everything the player experiences is discretised into frames
identities.needs: [has Label3D [has], missing frame-rate (FPS) display alongside absolute frame count]
identities.relationships: utility display used alongside interactive scenes; reminds learner of the discrete substrate of 3D

identities.essence: A 3D label showing the player's current health, updated from GameManager.health_updated signal
identities.desire: To give the player a stable readout of fragility — a number that changes only when the world has acted on them
identities.critical_parameter: signal connection to GameManager — without it the display lies; with it, every change in health is mirrored instantly
identities.triggers: Damage events lower the number; healing raises it; map reload resets it; visibility ties health to context
identities.emerges: A small 3D readout becomes the player's contract with the game — what counts as harm is what changes this label
identities.needs: Label3D rendering [has], GameManager signal binding [has], reset on map enter [has]
identities.relationships: Companion to hits_reset_display in forces/Combat_Arena. Both are visual contracts between game state and player perception
identities.truth: A health display is not a stat — it is a promise that change has consequences and that the world keeps account.

identities.essence: A 3D readout that mirrors player health and reflects the reset state — companion display to health_display
identities.desire: To name the moment of reset as visible — to show that being hit and being whole are tracked, not assumed
identities.critical_parameter: GameManager signal binding — the display is only honest while connected
identities.triggers: Damage updates the value; restart restores baseline; visibility tracks active map context
identities.emerges: A readout that pairs with health_display to make state legible — together they read as a small instrument panel
identities.needs: Label3D [has], GameManager signal [has], reset behavior [has]
identities.relationships: Twin of health_display in forces/Combat_Arena. Same pattern, different role
identities.truth: A reset is not a return to nothing — it is the act of restoring an expected state, and the readout is the witness.

identities.essence: a cylinder that refuses regularity — CSG spheres bulge the walls at intervals, making geometry breathe
identities.desire: to feel depth warp — the tunnel contracts and expands, confusing distance perception
identities.critical_parameter: num_bulges — controls the lambda between hallway (F=order) and cave (E=chaos)
identities.triggers: changing num_bulges or bulge_max_radius rebuilds the entire tunnel with new distortion profile
identities.emerges: at high bulge counts the tunnel becomes organic, more cave than corridor — geometry becomes landscape
identities.needs: hollow mode not called by default — could be a toggle; complex_tunnel mode exists but unused
identities.relationships: contrasts with mobius_strip_altgeo (twisted surface); pairs with klein_bottle (closed manifold); prepares for hyperbolic_plane (constant negative curvature)
identities.truth: a corridor is just a cave with its chaos removed

identities.essence: p(u,v) = (R + v*w*cos(u/2))*cos(u), sin), v*w*sin(u/2) — the half-twist parametric surface
identities.desire: To be walked — one full loop and your orientation flips, a second loop restores it, and you realize the surface has one side
identities.critical_parameter: the u/2 in cos(u/2) — this single half-angle is the entire twist, the difference between a cylinder and a Mobius strip
identities.triggers: Wall-walk collision layer enables lizard-feet adhesion; completing a loop flips the player's up-vector
identities.emerges: The disorientation of walking a non-orientable surface — you cannot tell which side you are on because there is only one side
identities.needs: VR wall-walk [has], orientation indicator [missing], loop-completion detection [missing]
identities.relationships: Guest from alternative_geometries sequence; contrasts Euclidean assumptions of all other maps
identities.truth: The Mobius strip does not have two sides — it has one side and the persistent illusion of two.

identities.essence: CSG boolean(sphere, cylinder, box) + FastNoiseLite displacement -> organic cave interior with floating orbs
identities.desire: to step inside a living space where walls breathe, tunnels curve, and crystals grow from nothing — architecture without architects
identities.critical_parameter: organic_strength — controls how much noise deforms the base geometry; at 0 it is a sphere, at 1 it is a cave
identities.triggers: regenerate_space() creates a new random interior; interactive orbs float with tween-driven gentle oscillation
identities.emerges: CSG boolean subtraction of noisy spheres from the shell creates doorways and alcoves that feel intentional but are accidental
identities.needs: CSG-to-mesh baking [has]; floating orbs [has]; atmospheric lighting [has]; VR regenerate trigger [missing]
identities.relationships: paired with branching_growth_algorithm in PG_Branching_Growth; contrasts deterministic growth with noise-sculpted space
identities.truth: an organic space is not designed from outside — it is what remains after noise has eaten away at geometry from within

identities.essence: growth_seeds -> RhizomaticMazeGenerator -> path_network -> organic tunnel meshes with noise displacement — Deleuze's rhizome as architecture
identities.desire: to wander a non-hierarchical tunnel network where every path leads to more paths, with no center and no dead ends that feel final
identities.critical_parameter: branch_probability (0.7) — controls how often paths fork; at 1.0 the network explodes, at 0 it is a single corridor
identities.triggers: generate_rhizomatic_maze() builds the full system in 6 phases; regenerate_maze() creates a new seed and rebuilds everything
identities.emerges: merge_threshold causes independent growth paths to fuse into loops, creating the non-hierarchical topology that defines a rhizome
identities.needs: organic tunnel meshes [has]; trimesh collision [has]; navigation waypoints [has]; VR exploration [has]; growth animation [missing]
identities.relationships: paired with mirror_cellular_texture_for_3d in PG_Mirrored_Patterns; contrasts with maze_generation (tree-structured vs rhizomatic)
identities.truth: a rhizome has no beginning and no end — it is always in the middle, between things, a line of flight

identities.essence: recursive branching with lateral reconnection — each new node grows from a random parent with direction = lerp(random, away_from_center, 1 - growth_direction_randomness), then probabilistically connects to nearby existing nodes
identities.desire: to grow a structure that has no center and no hierarchy — a rhizome where any point can connect to any other point, undermining tree-shaped thinking
identities.critical_parameter: connection_probability — at 0 the structure is a tree (hierarchical), at 1.0 every nearby node reconnects (rhizomatic), the transition is where Deleuze meets graph theory
identities.triggers: generate_structure builds the node/connection arrays; draw_structure renders CylinderMesh branches between connected nodes; regenerate() clears and regrows
identities.emerges: lateral connections create cycles in an otherwise tree-shaped growth, producing a network topology that resists reduction to any single root or trunk
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [missing]
identities.relationships: appears in GT_Network_Analysis as a Deleuze-Guattari-inspired contrast to hierarchical graph algorithms; challenges the tree assumption in tarjan and kosaraju
identities.truth: a rhizome has no beginning and no end — only middles, and every connection is as legitimate as every other

identities.essence: for i in range(4): cube.position = Vector3(0, 0, i × spacing) — four pickup cubes arranged as a linear array in the Z direction, each labeled [i]
identities.desire: to walk alongside an array — to see [0], [1], [2], [3] as physical objects in space and understand that an index is a distance, that traversal is movement
identities.critical_parameter: spacing — at 1.0 the cubes are adjacent and the array feels compact; at 2.0 they feel like separate objects; the default 1.0 makes index=position visible
identities.triggers: picking up a cube removes it from the array visualization, making the gap visible — the array has a hole where the index used to be
identities.emerges: the pink label color (light pink, Color(1.0, 0.7, 0.8)) subtly codes the array as soft rather than rigid, echoing the project's queer aesthetic
identities.needs: pickup cubes [has]; Label3D index labels [has]; no interactivity beyond grabbing [missing slider or button]; apply_grid_config supports count/spacing/label overrides [has]
identities.relationships: simpler than grid_2d_4x4 (one dimension vs two); appears in Tutorial_Row alongside xyz_coordinates; precedes grid_2d_4x4 in the tutorial sequence
identities.truth: an array is space made countable — column_3_z makes the abstract concept of an index into a physical position you can walk to

identities.essence: for x in range(4): for z in range(4): cube.position = Vector3(x, 0, z) with label "[x, z]" — a 4×4 grid of pickup cubes where each cube's position equals its index, paired with a binary table that shows the same data as 1s and 0s
identities.desire: to navigate a 2D array by walking it — to move from [0,0] to [3,3] and feel that two-dimensional indexing is a spatial act, not a notational one; and when you pick up a cube, to watch its slot turn to 0 in the binary table
identities.critical_parameter: show_binary_table — when true, a BinaryTableDisplay appears beside the grid showing the same 4×4 structure as a matrix of 0s and 1s; removing cubes live-updates the table, making the array-as-data-structure visible
identities.triggers: picking up any cube fires tree_exiting → _on_cube_removed(x,z) → grid_data[x][z] = 0 → binary_table.set_cell(x, z, 0) — the physical act of grabbing an object updates the data representation in real time
identities.emerges: students discover that the grid is not just a physical arrangement but a data structure — removing a cube is setting a value in a 2D array, and the binary table makes the data model visible alongside the spatial model
identities.needs: pickup cubes with grab physics [has]; Label3D index labels [has]; BinaryTableDisplay [has when show_binary_table=true]; pulsar_visualizer [external, in same map]; gridagent [external, in same map]; no VR slider controls [missing]
identities.relationships: extends column_3_z to 2 dimensions; precedes grid_3d_4x4x4; binary table connects to pulsar_visualizer (radio signal as 2D array); appears with gridagent in Tutorial_2D_Build
identities.truth: a 2D array is space folded into coordinates — this artifact makes coordinates walkable positions, proving that the abstract address [x,z] is always a location in space

identities.essence: for x,y,z in range(4)³: cube.position = Vector3(x,y,z) with label "[x,y,z]" — 64 pickup cubes forming a solid 4×4×4 volume where every position is labeled with its three-dimensional index
identities.desire: to climb inside a three-dimensional array — to reach up and grab a cube at [2,3,1] and feel that three numbers describe a unique place in space that only you can occupy at that moment
identities.critical_parameter: spacing — at 1.0m the cubes form a compact volume you can reach into; increasing spacing makes the array a sparse structure you must move through rather than reach across
identities.triggers: picking up cubes physically empties cells from the volume — the 3D array becomes a sculpture with negative space carved by interaction
identities.emerges: students discover that volumetric indexing requires physical intuition that 2D indexing does not — you must think in three directions simultaneously, and your body knows how to do this even when your mind struggles
identities.needs: pickup cubes [has]; Label3D [x,y,z] labels [has]; no-depth-test labels ensure always-readable index [has]; apply_grid_config supports size_x/y/z/spacing overrides [has]; no live data visualization companion [missing]
identities.relationships: extends grid_2d_4x4 to 3 dimensions; final step in the 1D→2D→3D spatial array progression; connects to voxelnoise (3D grid with noise values) and grid_3d in the grid_editor sequence
identities.truth: a three-dimensional array is the minimum structure needed to represent volumetric space — every 3D game world, CT scan, and weather simulation is an indexed cube of values

identities.essence: for i in range(4): cube.position = Vector3(i × spacing, 0, 0) with label "[i]" — a 1D array of four pickup cubes along the X axis, backed by a 1-row BinaryTableDisplay that turns to 0 when a cube is grabbed
identities.desire: to walk along an array in the X direction and feel that index increases as you move right — to then grab a cube and see the binary table update, closing the loop between physical action and data representation
identities.critical_parameter: show_binary_table — when true, a 1-row × 4-column "array[i]" table hovers above the row; picking up cube [2] changes the table cell at column 2 from 1 to 0, showing that the cube is the data
identities.triggers: tree_exiting signal on each cube fires _on_cube_removed(index) → sets array_data[0][index] = 0 → calls binary_table.set_cell(0, index, 0) — every grab is a write operation to a 1D array
identities.emerges: the single-row binary table labeled "array[i]" makes explicit that a row of objects IS an array — the visualization and the physical layout are the same data structure rendered in two different media
identities.needs: pickup cubes [has]; Label3D index labels [has]; BinaryTableDisplay [has]; apply_grid_config supports count/spacing/label overrides [has]; no VR controls beyond grabbing [missing]
identities.relationships: same architecture as column_3_z but oriented along X instead of Z, and with binary table companion; both appear in Tutorial_2D_Build to show X and Z axes as independent array dimensions; precedes grid_2d_4x4
identities.truth: a 1D array is a line of values — row_3_x makes this literal by arranging physical objects along an axis and labeling them with their distance from the origin

identities.essence: a miniature 1:10 scale interactive diorama of the current map's grid — layout_data[z][x] = height rendered as stacked cubes you can grab, move, and stack to reshape the terrain in real time
identities.desire: to make the 2D array that defines every map touchable — to hold the data structure in your hands, see indices as spatial coordinates, and feel that editing an array cell is moving a physical block
identities.critical_parameter: max_model_size — the model dynamically scales so any map fits within this bounding dimension (default 1.0m); a 10×10 map = 0.1m cells, a 20×15 map = 0.05m cells
identities.triggers: dropping a GridModelCube fires cube_dropped → GridModel calls structure_component.stack_remove(from) + stack_add(to) → the real terrain rebuilds; structure_component.cube_changed updates the model back
identities.emerges: students discover that the map IS a 2D array — every column is an address [x,z], every height is a value, and reshaping terrain is just writing to array cells
identities.needs: GridSystem in group "grid_system" [runtime]; GridStructureComponent with enable_editing/stack_add/stack_remove [has]; GridModelCube pickable [has]; XRToolsPickable [framework]
identities.relationships: builds on grid_2d_4x4 (2D array with labels); extends grid_editor concept (miniature ↔ fullscale); connects to GridSystem (the actual map renderer)
identities.truth: a map is a 2D array made walkable — this artifact reverses the abstraction, letting you hold the array and write to it by moving blocks

identities.essence: for each (row, col) in pulsar signal data: CylinderMesh(height = intensity × max_height, radius = tube_radius) positioned at (col×spacing_x, height/2, row×spacing_z) — every pulse's amplitude mapped to a physical glass tube height
identities.desire: to stand beside a radio signal from 2300 light-years away and see it as physical columns of glass — to understand that scientific data is an array and that arrays can be beautiful, spatial, and historically specific
identities.critical_parameter: max_height — scales all tube heights relative to the strongest signal pulse; at 0.25m the tallest tube reaches eye-level for seated VR; changing it transforms the data from a chart into an architectural landscape
identities.triggers: visualization_mode switches between tubes (CylinderMesh), lines (ImmediateMesh), and points, showing that the same data array can take different physical forms depending only on the rendering choice
identities.emerges: the sparse pattern of tall tubes versus short tubes reveals the pulsar's actual pulse shape — students encounter the mathematical structure of a neutron star's spin and atmosphere encoded in glass column heights
identities.needs: glass material [has]; glow material [has]; all three visualization modes [has]; no VR controls for changing visualization_mode [missing]; apply_grid_config not implemented [missing]
identities.relationships: compact form of pulsar_visualizer (which also shows the binary table); shares PulsarData static class for signal generation; appears in Tutorial_Pattern as the compact version; connects to grid_2d_4x4 (same data, different display)
identities.truth: scientific visualization is always a mapping from array index to physical property — tube height is signal intensity, and standing beside this mapping makes data science a spatial act

identities.essence: real pulsar radio signal data (B1919+21) → binary threshold at 0.25 → 2D array of 0s and 1s displayed as both a grid of numbers and a 3D glass bar chart — the same dataset rendered twice in two representational languages
identities.desire: to discover that Jocelyn Bell Burnell's pulsar discovery was a 2D array printed on a chart — to stand beside a radio signal visualized as glass tubes and understand that cosmic events are just arrays of numbers measured over time
identities.critical_parameter: the threshold (0.25 in PulsarData.get_binary_pulsar_sample) — above this value the signal is 1, below it is 0; changing it would alter what counts as a "pulse" and reveals that binary representation requires a decision about where to draw the line
identities.triggers: the glass tubes in pulsar_glass_tubes render signal amplitude as height — a tall tube means strong radio signal at that moment; the binary table beside it shows the same data after thresholding, making information loss from digitization visible
identities.emerges: students realize that the same phenomenon (pulsing neutron star) looks completely different in analogue (tube heights) vs digital (binary table) representation — and that arrays are always a choice about which values to keep
identities.needs: BinaryTableDisplay [has]; PulsarGlassTubes [has]; info panel with Label3D [has]; no VR interactive controls [missing]; apply_grid_config supports table_rows/cols/show_info [has]
identities.relationships: uses PulsarData static class for signal generation; pairs with pulsar_compact (glass tubes only, compact form); appears in Tutorial_2D_Build alongside grid_2d_4x4 to show arrays as measurement
identities.truth: the first discovered pulsar was initially called LGM-1 (Little Green Men) because the signal's regularity seemed artificial — arrays make the cosmic seem engineered, and engineered arrays can make data seem natural

identities.essence: four rows of 16 colored bars sort simultaneously using Bubble, Insertion, Selection, and Merge — each row animates one comparison/swap per tick so you can watch algorithms race
identities.desire: to see that sorting is not one thing but many strategies, each with a different rhythm — bubble plods, insertion slides, selection scans, merge conquers — and to feel the difference in your body as you watch them finish at different times
identities.critical_parameter: step_speed — controls ticks per second; at low speed you see every comparison, at high speed you see the emergent motion patterns of each algorithm
identities.triggers: SHUFFLE resets all rows to the same random permutation; RUN toggles continuous stepping; STEP advances one tick manually; SPEED slider adjusts tick rate
identities.emerges: merge sort finishes first almost every time, bubble sort last — the visual proof is more convincing than any Big-O lecture because you watched it happen
identities.needs: RackTemplates panel [has]; 4x16 bar grid [has]; per-algorithm state machines [has]; green flash on completion [has]
identities.relationships: complements sort_algorithm_animation in primitives (single algorithm focus) by showing comparison; feeds into complexity analysis artifacts
identities.truth: sorting algorithms are strategies for restoring order — watching four strategies race reveals that the question is never "does it work" but "how does it think"

identities.essence: strategy.step(grid) where strategy in {rule_switching, memory, gradient, pure_ca, downward_columns}
identities.desire: To grow furniture from rules — watch a chair emerge from a seed through five different CA strategies
identities.critical_parameter: strategy_type — each of five strategies produces fundamentally different growth morphologies
identities.triggers: Switching strategy → same seed, completely different chair; 30 generations → growth halts, form is final
identities.emerges: Chair-like forms from volumetric CA — no furniture geometry was specified, only growth rules
identities.needs: VR buttons [has via UI], speed slider [has], strategy switcher [has], Label3D [has]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_ExpandingSpace. Demonstrates that CA rules can be design tools, not just simulations.
identities.truth: A chair is a convergent form — different rules find it because sitting demands it.

identities.essence: next_cell = wolfram_rule(left, center, right) extruded as walkable bridge
identities.desire: To be crossed — a 1D automaton made physical, each row of cubes a generation you walk through
identities.critical_parameter: rule (0-255) — each Wolfram rule number produces a completely different bridge topology
identities.triggers: Rule 30 → chaotic, broken path; Rule 110 → structured walkway; random initial row → organic variation
identities.emerges: Walkable architecture from an 8-bit number — bridges, walls, gaps appear from three-neighbor logic
identities.needs: VR rule selector [missing], speed control [missing], collision [has]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_GameOfLife. Contrasts with ca_columns (1D→bridge vs 2D→towers). Precedes ca_rule_explorer.
identities.truth: A bridge built by a rule — you walk on computation.

identities.essence: 2D Game of Life stacked as 3D history — each generation becomes a new vertical layer
identities.desire: To grow a city of columns from a flat seed, then release walkers to erode and reshape it
identities.critical_parameter: rule_born/rule_survive — the Life variant determines whether columns are sparse towers or dense walls
identities.triggers: Generation completes → walkers spawn on top and begin stochastic erosion/deposition cycle
identities.emerges: Architectural forms from Life rules; walker erosion carves arches and bridges no one planned
identities.needs: VR rule controls [missing], walker parameter sliders [missing], density control [missing]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_GameOfLife. Contrasts with ca_bridge (1D rule → bridge vs 2D rule → columns). Unlocks CellularAutomata3DStacked.
identities.truth: Stack time as space and a flat automaton becomes architecture.

identities.essence: growth_tip += attractor_force / distance^2, with stochastic branching
identities.desire: To reach — tendrils seeking invisible attractors, branching when the signal is ambiguous
identities.critical_parameter: attractor_strength — how powerfully distant goals bend the growth direction
identities.triggers: Many attractors → dense bush; few → sparse reaching arms; high branch_probability → fractal explosion
identities.emerges: Root-like, vascular networks from simple force-toward-goal logic — no branching pattern was specified
identities.needs: VR attractor controls [missing], growth speed slider [missing]
identities.relationships: Contrasts with line_network_ca (random vs directed growth). Feeds into CA_BeyondBinary.
identities.truth: Growth toward a goal, with noise, is enough to produce every vascular pattern in nature.

identities.essence: S → I with P(infection) * infected_neighbors; I → R with P(recovery) — the SIR model on a 3D grid
identities.desire: To spread — watch infection ripple outward from patient zero, then the green wave of recovery follow
identities.critical_parameter: INFECTION_RATE vs RECOVERY_RATE — their ratio determines whether the epidemic burns out or persists
identities.triggers: High infection rate → explosive spread; high recovery → quick burnout; few initial infected → slow simmer
identities.emerges: Epidemic wavefronts, herd immunity boundaries, and spatial clustering from two probabilities
identities.needs: VR rate sliders [missing], reset button [missing], SIR count display [has via get_disease_counts]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_EdgeOfChaos. Extends PulsingCA (pulsing spheres for visual drama).
identities.truth: Two probabilities and a grid of neighbors — this is how pandemics actually work.

identities.essence: growth_frontier + parent_connection = branching line network
identities.desire: To sprout tendrils in all directions, each new cell tracing a luminous thread back to its parent
identities.critical_parameter: growth_probability — controls how aggressively the frontier expands
identities.triggers: Low growth_probability produces sparse, tree-like networks; high values create dense tangles
identities.emerges: Organic vascular structures — no branching logic was written, yet branches appear from random walk growth
identities.needs: VR growth controls [missing], color gradient adjustment [missing]
identities.relationships: Feeds from BaseCA. Contrasts with ca_growth_network (attractor-directed vs random). Introduces CA_Introduction.
identities.truth: Connect each new cell to a neighbor and a network appears — ancestry creates structure.

identities.essence: cell(t+1) = cell(t) * (1 - k) + avg(neighbors) * k + noise — local averaging with perturbation
identities.desire: To settle into consensus regions, then be disturbed — watch opinion clusters form and dissolve
identities.critical_parameter: INTERACTION_STRENGTH (0.1) — how fast cells converge toward their neighbors' average
identities.triggers: High interaction → rapid homogenization into uniform zones; randomness prevents total consensus
identities.emerges: Domain boundaries and cluster formation from simple averaging — phase separation without physics
identities.needs: VR interaction/randomness sliders [missing], diversity readout [has via get_pattern_diversity]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_EdgeOfChaos. Demonstrates self-organization as the CA analogue of social consensus.
identities.truth: Average with your neighbors and add noise — domains form, boundaries emerge, organization happens without an organizer.

identities.essence: vertex(t+1) = evolve(mode, neighbors) where mode in {CA, random_walk, hill_seeking}
identities.desire: To deform a sphere three different ways — watch topology warp under CA birth/death, random drift, and gravitational attraction
identities.critical_parameter: evolution_mode — switches between three fundamentally different deformation algorithms on the same mesh
identities.triggers: Mode switch → sphere resets and begins new deformation; iteration limit → evolution halts, form is frozen
identities.emerges: Organic, tumor-like growths on a sphere surface from vertex-level CA rules that know nothing about shape
identities.needs: VR mode selector [missing], iteration control [missing], keyboard input [has]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_SoftRules. Demonstrates CA on non-planar topology — contrasts with flat grid automata.
identities.truth: The same rules on a sphere produce forms no flat grid ever could — topology is a hidden variable.

identities.essence: 1D elementary cellular automaton on a texture — Wolfram rules applied to a scrolling image. Three-neighbor lookup, 8-bit rule encoding, 256 possible universes. Time flows as pixel rows.
identities.desire: To scroll when grabbed — grab_paper signals toggle scroll_on, making the automaton advance. Rules mutate stochastically (rule_change_chance) producing mid-stream phase transitions.
identities.critical_parameter: start_rule (Wolfram number 0-255) — determines which of the 256 possible 1D automata runs; rule_change_chance — probability of spontaneous rule mutation per step
identities.triggers: grab_paper_grabbed → scroll_on = true, automaton advances; grab_paper_dropped → scroll_on = false; timer → _update_automaton each update_interval
identities.emerges: Chaotic or structured patterns depending on the rule — Rule 30 produces noise, Rule 110 produces computation, Rule 90 produces Sierpinski triangles. Rule switches create visible phase boundaries in the scrolling texture.
identities.needs: VR grab interaction [has] via GrabPaper parent, rule selector UI [missing], zoom control [missing]
identities.relationships: The grabbable paper version of the 1D CA — child of cellular_automata_grabable.tscn, which wraps it in a GrabPaper with edge profile. Sibling to cellular_automata_2d (grid life) and rule_30_110 (gravity visualization).
identities.truth: Eight bits encode a universe. The distance between noise and thought is one lookup table — same input format, same three neighbors, radically different outputs.

identities.essence: Conway's Game of Life on a 20x20 toroidal grid — birth/survival/death rules applied per generation. Cube scenes instantiated for live cells, shader-colored by age. Gliders, blinkers, and blocks seeded at init.
identities.desire: To evolve autonomously — _process advances generations at generation_interval, applying the four Conway rules. Dying cells shrink, newborns glow, aged cells redden.
identities.critical_parameter: generation_interval — seconds between state transitions; grid_size — dimensions of the toroidal world (20x20 = 400 cells)
identities.triggers: _ready → initialize_grid + seed patterns + create_cell_visuals; generation_timer → update_generation → count_neighbors → apply rules → update_cell_visuals
identities.emerges: Gliders traverse the grid, blinkers oscillate, blocks persist. From four rules on a flat grid: movement, oscillation, stability, and extinction — the full taxonomy of dynamical behavior.
identities.needs: VR cell toggling [missing], pattern library selector [missing], generation speed slider [missing]
identities.relationships: The 2D step between cellular_automata (1D scrolling) and cellular_automata_3d (volumetric). Shares the RecursiveEmergence sequence with lattice_gas_automata — same grid, different interpretation.
identities.truth: Four rules. That is the entire program. Everything else — gliders, guns, Turing completeness — is consequence, not design.

identities.essence: 3D cellular automaton on a 12^3 grid — 26-neighbor Moore neighborhood, four rule sets (Life3D, Crystal Growth, Erosion, Diffusion). MultiMesh renders live cells as colored spheres; dying cells flash red before removal.
identities.desire: To cycle through rule regimes — every rule_interval seconds the automaton switches rules and reinitializes, showing how the same grid substrate produces coral, crystal, erosion, and diffusion under different transition tables.
identities.critical_parameter: current_rule (Rule3D enum) — selects which birth/survival/death thresholds apply; grid_size (12) — cube dimensions; max_generations (100) — simulation cap before halt
identities.triggers: _process → generation_timer fires at generation_interval → generate_next_3d_generation; rule_timer → switch_3d_rule → reinitialize; GenerationControl/DensityIndicator → animated height indicators
identities.emerges: Forms that the flat law never predicted — 2D rules given volume discover architecture. Crystal Growth seeds from center outward, Erosion strips sparse cells, Diffusion bridges corners. Same counting, different thresholds, radically different morphology.
identities.needs: VR rule selector [missing], generation playback [missing], cell state inspection [missing]
identities.relationships: The volumetric extension of cellular_automata_2d (2D grid life). Paired with cellular_automata_3d_stacked (stacked generation history). Appears in RecursiveEmergence_Cellular_Automata_3D map.
identities.truth: The automaton does not know it has depth — it only counts neighbors. But depth knows it has the automaton. A flat law, given volume, discovers forms it was never told to make.

identities.essence: layer(n+1) = life_rules(layer(n)) with outward→upward phase transition
identities.desire: To extrude a flat Game of Life into a standing structure — watch 2D rules build 3D form
identities.critical_parameter: GrowthPhase transition at generation 4 — switches from horizontal expansion to vertical extrusion
identities.triggers: Phase OUT → spreading footprint; phase UP → columns rising; generation 10 → growth halts
identities.emerges: Architectural columns and cantilevers from the phase transition between horizontal and vertical growth
identities.needs: VR phase controls [missing], speed control [missing]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_AgentsCircuits. Builds on ca_columns (implicit stacking vs explicit phase control).
identities.truth: The same rules in two phases — spread then rise — produce architecture from biology.

identities.essence: square_layer(n) → ca_prune(edge, isolation, random) → tree silhouette
identities.desire: To grow upward layer by layer, pruning itself into a tree shape through local elimination rules
identities.critical_parameter: edge_pruning_chance — controls how aggressively corners are carved, shaping the crown profile
identities.triggers: High isolation_pruning → skeletal branches; low → dense canopy; changing base_size → bonsai vs oak
identities.emerges: Tree-like silhouettes from rectangular layers and three simple removal rules — no tree model was coded
identities.needs: VR pruning sliders [missing], growth speed control [missing]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_ExpandingSpace. Contrasts with lsystem_tree (subtractive CA vs additive grammar).
identities.truth: A tree is what remains when you remove everything that isn't tree.

identities.essence: per_row_rule[y] = random(0..255); cell = wolfram(rule[y], neighbors)
identities.desire: To be a crossroads of rules — each row obeys a different Wolfram number, creating layered conflict
identities.critical_parameter: rule_change_interval — how often rules re-randomize, controlling stability vs perpetual novelty
identities.triggers: Every 10 turns all rules re-randomize → the entire pattern language shifts; collision toggles walkability
identities.emerges: Interference patterns where different rule regimes collide at row boundaries — moiré-like zones of order
identities.needs: VR rule display [missing], speed control [missing], collision [has]
identities.relationships: Extends ca_bridge (single rule → many rules). Feeds into CA_ExpandingSpace.
identities.truth: When every row speaks a different rule language, the boundaries become the most interesting places.

identities.essence: Lattice gas automaton on a 20x20 grid with 8 velocity directions — particles propagate, collide (head-on pairs scatter perpendicular), and produce emergent fluid dynamics. Macroscopic density, velocity, and pressure computed from microscopic boolean states.
identities.desire: To demonstrate that Navier-Stokes emerges from counting — particles obey trivial collision rules, yet the lattice forgets it is discrete. Vortices form. Turbulence cascades.
identities.critical_parameter: grid_size (20) — lattice resolution; velocity_directions — 8 compass vectors defining the HPP/FHP-style lattice connectivity
identities.triggers: _process → step_timer fires every 0.1s → update_lattice (collision + propagation + macroscopic calculation) → visualize all three layers
identities.emerges: Four visualization layers: grid base (static), particle spheres (colored by direction), flow arrows (oriented by local velocity), density pillars (height = local density). Fluid behavior visible at macro scale from micro rules.
identities.needs: VR obstacle placement [missing], flow speed control [missing], lattice topology selector [missing]
identities.relationships: Bridges cellular automata to fluid dynamics — same grid logic as cellular_automata_2d, different interpretation. Appears in both RecursiveEmergence_Cellular_Automata_2D and RecursiveEmergence_Lattice_Gas_Automata maps.
identities.truth: The continuous is a hallucination performed by the discrete at sufficient scale. Matter performing smoothness through sheer repetition.

identities.essence: health(cell) -= decay_if_near_player; health += regrow_rate * healthy_neighbors
identities.desire: To crumble under your feet and heal behind you — architecture that remembers your weight
identities.critical_parameter: decay_speed vs regrow_speed — the ratio determines whether the bridge survives your crossing
identities.triggers: Standing still → hole opens beneath you; moving fast → bridge barely notices; no player → full restoration
identities.emerges: Path memory — the bridge records where you walked as a fading scar of transparency
identities.needs: VR parameter controls [missing], player tracking [has via group lookup], collision [has]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_ExpandingSpace. Extends ca_bridge (static structure → responsive architecture).
identities.truth: Architecture that reacts to presence is architecture that is alive.

identities.essence: hex_cell(t+1) = life_rule(6_neighbors) stacked vertically — terrain from time
identities.desire: To grow a hexagonal landscape you can walk on, each generation a new geological layer
identities.critical_parameter: random_flip — injects noise into deterministic rules, controlling the chaos-order boundary
identities.triggers: High random_flip → turbulent terrain; low → smooth plateaus; changing radius → intimate vs epic scale
identities.emerges: Walkable terrain with caves and overhangs from stacking hex Life generations with noise
identities.needs: VR random_flip controller [has], Label3D [has], collision [has]
identities.relationships: Extends CA_BeyondBinary (hex grid vs square). Feeds into CA_ExpandingSpace (3D from 2D).
identities.truth: Six neighbors instead of eight — the shape of the neighborhood reshapes the world.

identities.essence: cell(t+1) = born/survive(neighbors) with four-fold symmetry enforcement
identities.desire: To weave itself — a living carpet whose patterns breathe and shift like textile memory
identities.critical_parameter: rule_border_born/survive vs rule_inner_born/survive — two rulesets create the border-interior tension
identities.triggers: Switching random_seed reshuffles initial conditions; changing border vs inner rules shifts the visual dialect entirely
identities.emerges: Intricate symmetric textile patterns from the interplay of two CA rulesets and forced mirror symmetry
identities.needs: VR parameter controls [missing], auto-play toggle [has via auto_step]
identities.relationships: Contrasts with mirrored_cellular_automata (stochastic symmetry vs deterministic). Feeds into CA_Introduction.
identities.truth: Symmetry imposed on local rules transforms noise into ornament — the rug designs itself.

identities.essence: Side-by-side elementary CA comparison — Rule 30 (chaotic) and Rule 110 (Turing-complete) visualized as dual MultiMesh grids. Each generation appends a row of colored cubes; Rule 30 in warm chaos tones, Rule 110 in cool complexity gradients.
identities.desire: To show that eight bits separate noise from thought — same three-neighbor input, same pattern-to-state lookup, but Rule 30 produces cryptographic randomness while Rule 110 carries logic. Both advance in lockstep.
identities.critical_parameter: grid_width (51) — cell count per row; max_generations (30) — vertical depth before reset; generation_speed (0.3s) — time between row advances
identities.triggers: _process → generation_timer fires → advance_generation → apply_rule_30/apply_rule_110 → visualize both; reset at max_generations → reinitialize seeds
identities.emerges: Rule 30's left half: turbulent triangles, no period, no compression. Rule 110's right half: structured gliders, localized structures, proven universal computation. The visual gap between them is the gap between entropy and information.
identities.needs: VR rule number selector [missing], generation scrubber [missing], side-by-side parameter comparison [missing]
identities.relationships: Focused companion to cellular_automata (1D scrolling texture) — same Wolfram rule engine, different visualization strategy. Appears in RecursiveEmergence_Rule_30_110 map under rule_30_110_gravity lookup.
identities.truth: The distance between noise and thought is one lookup table apart. Rule 30 generates chaos. Rule 110 generates computation. Same format. Same input size. Radically different outputs.

identities.essence: pyramid(depth) = 5 * pyramid(depth-1) — top + four corners, recursively
identities.desire: To be climbed and understood — a fractal mountain where every face is itself
identities.critical_parameter: depth — each increment multiplies complexity by 5, from 5 cubes to 3125
identities.triggers: Depth 1 → five cubes; depth 4 → a mountain of self-similar structure; @tool → live preview in editor
identities.emerges: Gaps and voids at every scale — the pyramid is more hole than solid, yet structurally coherent
identities.needs: VR depth control [missing], scale adjustment [missing]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_AgentsCircuits. Bridges fractals sequence to cellularautomata — Sierpinski via recursion, not CA rules.
identities.truth: Five copies of yourself, arranged just so, and you contain yourself forever.

identities.essence: B5+/S4+ on a 3D grid → density texture → FogVolume — CA rules become visible atmosphere
identities.desire: To be walked through — fog that has opinions about where it clumps, thinning and thickening by local rules
identities.critical_parameter: smooth_factor and birth/survival thresholds (B5/S4) — control whether fog dissipates or aggregates
identities.triggers: High survival threshold → fog evaporates; low → dense permanent clouds; grid resolution → fine mist vs chunky blocks
identities.emerges: Cloud-like formations from binary CA rules — no fluid dynamics, yet the fog moves like weather
identities.needs: VR density controls [missing], rule parameter sliders [missing]
identities.relationships: Feeds into CA_EdgeOfChaos. Unique in using CA to drive Godot's FogVolume system directly.
identities.truth: Fog is a cellular automaton — local density rules produce clouds no one shaped.

identities.essence: x_{n+1} = f(x_n, params); for Lorenz/Clifford/De Jong/Bedhead/Svensson/Ikeda, iterate a nonlinear map. The trajectory is bounded but never repeats — a structure that exists without converging.
identities.desire: To make chaos look like a place — velocity-colored trails turn the attractor into a sculpted ribbon you can walk around in VR, while the Lyapunov exponent reads out divergence as you adjust parameters.
identities.critical_parameter: attractor_type (which map) + max_points (memory budget for the visible trail) + parameter sliders that lerp toward target_params for smooth basin-to-basin morphing.
identities.triggers: _process tick → iterate the map iterations_per_frame times → append to _trail_points → rebuild ImmediateMesh ribbon → update Lyapunov readout
identities.emerges: A stable shape from a divergent process — nearby trajectories separate exponentially (positive Lyapunov), yet the cloud they trace settles into the same skeleton every time.
identities.needs: VR parameter sliders [missing], type-cycle button [missing]
identities.relationships: Belongs in fractals as the chaos-side of self-similarity (attractors have fractal dimension); pairs with logistic_map and lorenz_demo in the chaos arc.
identities.truth: An attractor is a memory the system can't escape — every orbit forgets where it started but remembers what shape it lives inside.

identities.essence: Snell's law visualized — white beam enters prism, refracts into 7-color fan by wavelength-dependent angle
identities.desire: to stand inside the album cover and watch white light split into a rainbow you can almost touch
identities.critical_parameter: fan_length — controls how far the spectrum spreads, making refraction feel gentle or dramatic
identities.triggers: none — static sculpture, always present, always splitting
identities.emerges: the glow/bloom system makes the beams feel volumetric even though they are 1-pixel ImmediateMesh lines
identities.needs: VR interaction [missing]; adjustable prism angle [missing]; Label3D [missing]
identities.relationships: contrasts with rainbow (full arc vs linear split); precedes spectrum_forest (spatial color mapping)
identities.truth: white light is not the absence of color — it is every color compressed into one, waiting for a boundary to reveal the multiplicity

identities.essence: grid(width, height) of BoxMesh bricks colored sequentially from a named palette — running bond pattern
identities.desire: to see a color palette become architecture, each brick a swatch in a wall you can walk alongside
identities.critical_parameter: palette — selects from 20 named palettes (starry_night to industrial_brutalism), redefining the wall's emotional register
identities.triggers: apply_grid_config can change dimensions, brick size, mortar, and palette at runtime — wall regenerates entirely
identities.emerges: the running bond offset (half-brick shift on odd rows) creates diagonal color rivers through the palette sequence
identities.needs: palette selection [has via config]; VR interaction [missing]; mortar color control [missing]
identities.relationships: depends on color_palettes.tres; contrasts with pillarcolorcollection (vertical vs horizontal color display)
identities.truth: a brick wall is a color sequence made solid — the mortar is the silence between notes

identities.essence: N rigid spheres sampled from named color palettes — physics + palette = chromatic rain
identities.desire: to toss, scatter, and watch colored balls pool and bounce, making palette differences visceral through physics
identities.critical_parameter: current_palette_index — switches the entire chromatic vocabulary; same physics, different visual language
identities.triggers: palette cycling recolors all balls instantly; falling below threshold respawns with new random palette color
identities.emerges: balls cluster by momentum into accidental color groupings that look curated but are pure physics
identities.needs: MultiMesh renderer [has]; palette cycling [has]; VR grab [missing]; turret integration [has]
identities.relationships: depends on color_palettes.tres; colorballs group lets turret find and shoot at them; feeds into brick_wall_factory as color source contrast
identities.truth: a color only becomes real when it has mass — palette theory means nothing until you can throw it

identities.essence: path_i(t) = f_type(t, params) where type in {spiral, wave, random, orbit, dna}
identities.desire: Walk through a hallway of flowing colored light tubes that follow mathematical paths
identities.critical_parameter: flow_speed — controls how fast color flows along the lines
identities.triggers: animation_speed modulates the parametric path evolution over time
identities.emerges: an immersive tunnel of living light from five basic curve equations
identities.needs: VR walkthrough [has], path type selection [missing]
identities.relationships: depends on ImmediateMesh line rendering; contrasts with hallway_scene (color tubes vs sine tubes); unlocks parametric curve visualization
identities.truth: Every flowing line is a parametric curve — a point moving through space according to equations.

identities.essence: RGB/CMY glass walls at angles — additive color mixing through transparency and emitted light overlap
identities.desire: to walk between colored glass partitions and see your shadow split into complementary colors on the floor
identities.critical_parameter: transparency — controls how much light passes through each wall; at 0.4 the mixing is visible but walls remain distinct
identities.triggers: none — static installation; color mixing happens through player movement and viewing angle
identities.emerges: walking through overlapping RGB walls creates white-ish zones where all three primaries combine — additive mixing proven by architecture
identities.needs: OmniLight3D per wall [has]; transparency [has]; VR walkthrough [has]; interactive wall rotation [missing]
identities.relationships: contrasts with albers_wall_gallery (subtractive paint vs additive light); follows dark_side_prism (spectrum split vs color recombination)
identities.truth: color mixing is not a formula — it is what happens when light from different sources arrives at the same place at the same time

identities.essence: palette_atlas — N palettes laid out as grabbable sticker grids, each sticker labeled with hex + nearest web color name
identities.desire: to pick up a color, read its name, and carry it across the room — making color portable and personal
identities.critical_parameter: sets_to_show — controls how many palettes are visible simultaneously, determining comparison density
identities.triggers: none at runtime — static grabbable display; XR pickup on each sticker via grab_paper.tscn
identities.emerges: the luminance-adaptive label contrast (dark text on light stickers, light on dark) makes every color readable without explicit design per palette
identities.needs: grab_paper.tscn XR pickup [has]; hex/name labels [has]; VR grab [has]; palette filtering [missing]
identities.relationships: depends on color_palettes.tres; follows pillarcolorcollection (viewing vs holding color); closest_web_color_name bridges digital hex to human language
identities.truth: naming a color does not capture it — but it makes the gap between name and experience visible

identities.essence: the path between two colors depends on which space you walk through
identities.desire: pick two colors, watch 16 cubes paint a gradient, toggle RGB/HSV and see the path change
identities.critical_parameter: interpolation mode — RGB walks a straight line in a cube, HSV walks an arc on a cylinder
identities.triggers: Color A/B sliders pick from 8 presets; Mode button toggles RGB/HSV; all trigger full recalculation
identities.emerges: RGB gradients can look muddy; HSV gradients pass through the rainbow — same endpoints, different journeys
identities.needs: RackTemplates panel [has]; BoxMesh gradient cubes [has]; Label3D mode display [has]
identities.relationships: sibling to subpixel_display (both explore color representation); feeds into colorspaces
identities.truth: Interpolation is not neutral — the space you choose shapes every color you pass through.

identities.essence: thin alias so the historical GridColorizer name still resolves
identities.desire: zero behaviour change after the substrate split
identities.critical_parameter: none — all behaviour delegated to GridColorMutator
identities.triggers: scene-load (existing tscn references this script path)
identities.emerges: the original behaviour, byte-for-byte, via the new shared base
identities.needs: GridColorMutator [present]
identities.relationships: GridColorMutator (parent); was the original mutator before

identities.essence: pillar_grid(rows, cols) colored from palette[i % palette.size()] — vertical color swatches as architectural columns
identities.desire: to walk a colonnade where each pillar is a different color, feeling palette relationships through spatial rhythm
identities.critical_parameter: current_palette_index — cycling palettes transforms the colonnade's mood while the geometry stays fixed
identities.triggers: cycle_to_next_palette() regenerates all pillars with the next palette; GameManager provides gradient palettes
identities.emerges: the grid layout creates sight-lines through columns where distant pillars optically mix with near ones
identities.needs: palette cycling [has]; pillar.tscn prefab [has]; VR palette selector [missing]; Label3D [missing]
identities.relationships: depends on color_palettes.tres and pillar.tscn; contrasts with brick_wall_factory (horizontal vs vertical); feeds into color_sets_overview (structured vs grabbable)
identities.truth: a column of color has gravity that a flat swatch does not — verticality makes color feel like it stands for something

identities.essence: hue(x) = remap(x, bounds) — 5000 vertical lines colored by x-position across the visible spectrum
identities.desire: to walk through a rain of color, each step shifting the hue around you from violet to red
identities.critical_parameter: line_count — at low counts the spectrum is sparse and abstract, at high counts it becomes an immersive curtain
identities.triggers: none at runtime — static procedural sculpture generated once from deterministic seed
identities.emerges: the density of lines creates an accidental fog effect where distant colors blend perceptually, demonstrating optical mixing
identities.needs: VR walkthrough [has]; line_count slider [missing]; spectrum range control [missing]
identities.relationships: contrasts with dark_side_prism (linear spectrum vs spatial spectrum); feeds into SpectrumVisualizer (animated spectrum vs static)
identities.truth: the spectrum is continuous but we discretize it into lines — the gaps between lines are the same lie as RGB

identities.essence: wavelength_to_color(lambda) animated between linear layout (physics) and circular layout (perception) — the spectrum closes into a wheel
identities.desire: to watch the visible spectrum bend from a line into a circle, magenta dots filling the gap that physics leaves empty
identities.critical_parameter: cycle_duration — controls how long you dwell in physics-mode vs perception-mode, pacing the conceptual shift
identities.triggers: time drives a continuous phase animation: 0-40% linear, 40-60% transition, 60-100% circular — no user input needed
identities.emerges: magenta dots appearing in the gap reveal that magenta is not a spectral color — it is the brain's invention to close the loop
identities.needs: auto-animation [has]; Label3D [missing]; VR pause/scrub [missing]; wavelength labels [missing]
identities.relationships: contrasts with spectrum_forest (spatial vs temporal spectrum); follows dark_side_prism (static split vs animated closure)
identities.truth: the color wheel is a lie the brain tells to make the spectrum feel complete — magenta is the seam

identities.essence: additive color mixing at the hardware level — red + green + blue = everything
identities.desire: drag three sliders, watch three bars glow, see the mixed color emerge above
identities.critical_parameter: emission_energy on each bar — intensity maps directly to channel value 0-1
identities.triggers: slider_moved on R/G/B sliders updates bar emission and combined quad
identities.emerges: understanding that white is all channels full, black is all off, and every color is a recipe
identities.needs: RackTemplates panel [has]; BoxMesh bars with emission [has]; QuadMesh combined swatch [has]
identities.relationships: feeds into gradient_interpolator (color mixing); sibling to colorspaces (both explore color representation)
identities.truth: Every pixel on every screen is three tiny lights pretending to be one color.

identities.essence: catalog(parts) + assembly(bonds, positions) -> molecular morphology
identities.desire: watch scattered atoms find each other and snap into bodies
identities.critical_parameter: assembly_name — switches between VRBody, Chair, entirely different topologies
identities.triggers: auto_cycle timer alternates float/assemble; JSON hot-reload rebuilds catalog live
identities.emerges: the moment of recognition when disordered parts coalesce into a legible form
identities.needs: VR grab on parts [missing], keyboard controls [has], auto-cycle [has]
identities.relationships: unlocks post-reductionist design thinking; depends on Part.tscn/assemblies.json; contrasts snap_cube_puzzle (fixed vs fluid assembly)
identities.truth: form is not imposed on matter — it is a conversation between catalog and constraint

identities.essence: CSG boolean operations (UNION, SUBTRACTION) on spheres, cylinders, and tori — generating radiolaria, spiky forms, lattice spheres, ringed forms, and pollen through procedural composition
identities.desire: to fill a grid with biological specimens that look grown rather than designed — each one a unique CSG sculpture you can walk around and inspect in VR
identities.critical_parameter: spikiness_probability — controls how many forms grow spines; at 0 all forms are smooth spheres, at 1.0 every specimen bristles with projections
identities.triggers: randi() % 6 selects form type per grid cell; randf() gates each sub-feature (bumps, spokes, pores); golden-ratio icosahedron vertices place spikes symmetrically
identities.emerges: the combination of random form selection and random feature gating means no two grids produce the same cabinet of specimens, yet all feel biologically plausible
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [missing]
identities.relationships: bridges soft body physics to affect theory in SoftBodies_Affect_Theory_Visualization; inspired by Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur
identities.truth: a radiolarian's skeleton is not engineered — it is what remains after surface tension, mineral deposition, and evolutionary pressure finish negotiating

identities.essence: documentation panel for Reynolds' 1987 boids algorithm — separation + alignment + cohesion described in text and connected to a live BoidManager instance
identities.desire: to read the three rules and immediately look up to see them happening — the gap between description and phenomenon collapsed into the same VR moment
identities.critical_parameter: show_algorithm — with algorithm text visible, learners read the rules while watching them; without it, the behavior looks like magic with no explanation
identities.triggers: the panel connects to the live BoidManager in the scene, so parameter changes in the manager are reflected in the UI context — explanation and simulation stay in sync
identities.emerges: the question "why does alignment make them look alive?" — the documentation exists to be outrun by the learner's own observation
identities.needs: [missing] no VR interaction; panel is 2D CanvasLayer projected into VR viewport — cannot be grabbed or repositioned by VR controller
identities.relationships: companion to boid_manager (documents what it simulates); boids_2d_in_3d projects this panel into a 3D viewport quad for VR placement
identities.truth: the rules are three lines of math; the flock is what those lines mean when they meet each other a thousand times per second

identities.essence: f_i = Σ(neighbor_j)[separate(i,j) + align(vel_j) + cohere(pos_j)] — three weighted averages over a local neighborhood
identities.desire: to reach out a VR hand and feel the flock split and reform around your arm — to be a boulder in a river of agency
identities.critical_parameter: interaction_radius — at zero, it's a particle cloud; past a threshold, a coherent organism crystallizes from the randomness
identities.triggers: left trigger attracts boids toward controller; right trigger repels — learner's body becomes a temporary leader with no followers bound by loyalty
identities.emerges: coordinated lane reversals, vortex rings, and split-rejoin events that no rule specifies — the flock invents maneuvers
identities.needs: [has] VR controller attract/repel via trigger; [missing] no sliders for separation/alignment/cohesion weights; no on-screen parameter display
identities.relationships: boids_aquarium wraps the same physics in a compact glass tank with sliders; boid_flocking adds the documentation UI; contrasts with FlowFieldMain (rules vs. field)
identities.truth: coordination is not agreement — it is geometry; close enough means you are already the same

identities.essence: population(t+1) = reproduce(survive(eat(move(population(t))))) with DNA crossover and mutation at each birth — evolution in a closed box
identities.desire: to watch a predator-prey cycle spike and crash and recover — to feel the ecosystem breathe and realize no agent understands the cycle, only you can see it
identities.critical_parameter: mutation_rate — at 0 the ecosystem either freezes in its starting configuration or collapses; at 0.1 adaptation keeps prey one step ahead of predators indefinitely
identities.triggers: balance_ecosystem() acts as a hidden stabilizer that respawns prey below 10 and weakens predators when they outnumber prey by 2:1 — remove it and the system collapses in minutes
identities.emerges: prey develop faster flee_weight and higher perception_radius over generations without explicit selection pressure — predation IS the selection pressure
identities.needs: [missing] no VR controls at all; prey_population, predator_population, and mutation_rate are hardcoded; learner cannot experiment with initial conditions
identities.relationships: synthesis artifact for the swarmintelligence sequence; combines local movement rules from boids with genetic memory from neuroevolution; previews machinelearning sequence's evolutionary algorithms
identities.truth: evolution has no goal — only the dead are wrong, and only the living get to try again

identities.essence: three modes — stigmergy (deposit/evaporate field), Ising phase transition (spin flip via Metropolis), attractor basins (gradient descent on potential landscape)
identities.desire: to push the Noise slider past the critical temperature and watch an ordered flock dissolve into chaos in real time — to hold the phase transition in your hand
identities.critical_parameter: coupling_strength — below the critical value spins are random (disordered phase); above it they spontaneously align (ordered phase); the exact threshold is where complexity peaks
identities.triggers: in PHASE_TRANSITION mode, the automated temperature sweep crosses the critical point and the order-parameter graph shows a sharp kink — the signature of a second-order transition
identities.emerges: in STIGMERGY mode, agents following their own collective trail spontaneously form rotating clusters — an ordered state nobody chose, arising from the instability of uniform randomness
identities.needs: [has] VR slider for Noise (temperature) and Coupling; [has] mode cycle button and reset button; [missing] no slider for agent_speed or deposit_rate
identities.relationships: generalizes the stigmergy mechanism of stigmergy_grid and AntColonyOptimization into abstract physics; shares Ising model concepts with phase_transition topics in chaos sequence; connects to attractor theory in neural networks
identities.truth: order is not imposed from outside — it falls into existence when local interactions exceed the noise floor

identities.essence: Forces as accumulating vectors — wind pushes, drag opposes, orbits emerge from radial attraction plus tangent velocity
identities.desire: To translate Shiffman's 2D Processing forces sketch into VR space, preserving the algorithm while making vectors graspable
identities.critical_parameter: drag and orbital_radius — drag chooses whether forces accumulate or settle; radius shifts orbit shape from circle to ellipse
identities.triggers: Zero drag gives runaway acceleration; high drag stalls motion into terminal velocity; orbit radius too small produces capture, too large produces escape
identities.emerges: A small set of independent force functions composes into trajectories that feel intentional, like physics knows what it wants
identities.needs: vector force accumulation [has], drag and gravity [has], orbital mechanics [has], VR sliders [has]
identities.relationships: NOC Ch.2 anchor artifact in forces/Newton's_Laws map. Companion to example_2_2_forces_mass_variation_vr (mass added)
identities.truth: A force is not a thing that pushes — it is a vector you decide to add. The motion is what the addition becomes over time.

identities.essence: Wind and drag applied to many balls of different masses — F=ma made visible as different responses to identical force
identities.desire: To turn the equation F=ma into a perceptual event — same wind pushes large and small differently, mass becomes legible as motion
identities.critical_parameter: wind_strength and drag_coefficient — together they decide whether mass differences read as separation or noise
identities.triggers: Zero wind makes mass invisible; strong wind separates masses by acceleration; high drag erases the differences over time
identities.emerges: A row of objects of varying mass under one wind becomes a histogram of inertia, sorted by acceleration response
identities.needs: per-ball mass [has], wind force application [has], drag force [has], VR sliders [has]
identities.relationships: Direct successor to example_2_1_forces_vr (adds mass). Anchor artifact in forces/Newton's_Laws map
identities.truth: Mass is not a number on a scale — it is the resistance that makes one body's response to a force differ from another's.

identities.essence: Gravity computed as a force scaled by each body's mass, revealing that all masses fall at the same acceleration
identities.desire: To enact Galileo's experiment — drop different masses, watch them stay together, see why F=mg cancels in the equation of motion
identities.critical_parameter: gravity_strength — the constant that proves itself constant by producing equal acceleration regardless of mass
identities.triggers: Default gravity reproduces Galileo's result; reducing gravity slows the fall but masses still descend together; reversing gravity inverts the demonstration
identities.emerges: The equivalence principle as visible event — heavy and light reach the floor together, the algebra confirmed by the eye
identities.needs: per-body mass [has], gravity force application [has], visible arrow comparison [has], VR sliders [has]
identities.relationships: NOC Ch.2 trilogy with example_2_1 and example_2_2. Anchor artifact in forces/Newton's_Laws map
identities.truth: Gravity treats mass as both source and target — and so cancels itself in motion, leaving acceleration alone to fall.

identities.essence: F_drag = -C * |v|^2 * v-hat. Drag opposes motion and scales with speed squared. Heavier objects fall faster through the same fluid.
identities.desire: To drop five balls of different masses into a blue fluid and watch the heavy ones punch through while the light ones float — mass as privilege in a resistive medium.
identities.critical_parameter: drag_coefficient — higher C means thicker fluid. It determines terminal velocity and how quickly the fluid swallows kinetic energy.
identities.triggers: VR sliders → adjust drag/gravity/depth in real time, Space → scatter movers sideways, R → reset, drag arrows appear when movers enter fluid
identities.emerges: Terminal velocity — each mover reaches a speed where gravity and drag balance. Heavier movers reach higher terminal velocity. The cyan drag arrows grow with speed.
identities.needs: VR rack panel with three sliders [has], drag arrow visualization [has], auto-reset timer [has]. Missing: density comparison overlay.
identities.relationships: Force decomposition like normal_force_demo. Lives in ForcesFoundations. Feeds into particle_systems (particles with drag). Contrasts with force_fields (area-based vs velocity-based forces).
identities.truth: Drag is the medium's memory of your velocity. The faster you move, the harder the world pushes back.

identities.essence: one massive attractor surrounded by movers — gravity-as-1/r² made visible with escape velocity and Roche-limit rings
identities.desire: feel the regimes — bound orbit, escape, tidal tear — as distinct states of the same physics
identities.critical_parameter: gravity strength and mover initial velocity — together they place each body in a regime
identities.triggers: _ready() spawns attractor + mover ring; _physics_process() integrates gravitational pulls between all bodies
identities.emerges: orbits, parabolic escapes, and Roche-stretched movers that visibly stretch as they near the boundary
identities.needs: gravity slider [present]; mode switch single/multi-body [present]; mover seed reset [present]
identities.relationships: forces-chapter origin for the gravity question revisited in example_4_1_single_particle_vr (multi-field) and chaos/strangeattractors
identities.truth: Gravity is a regime detector. The same equation produces an orbit, an escape, or a shredded mover depending on initial speed — physics is a multi-stable system.

identities.essence: Two bodies pulling each other via inverse-square gravitation, producing closed orbits, escapes, or collisions
identities.desire: To make the two-body problem visible — Kepler's elliptical solution emerges from F = G·m₁·m₂/r² applied symmetrically
identities.critical_parameter: gravitational_constant and initial tangential velocity — together they decide circular, elliptical, parabolic, or hyperbolic
identities.triggers: Low velocity collapses bodies into each other; tuned velocity yields stable ellipse; high velocity becomes escape trajectory
identities.emerges: Conic sections appear without being coded — the orbit shape is not chosen, it is what the algebra of mutual attraction does
identities.needs: per-body mass [has], inverse-square attraction force [has], trail visualization [has]
identities.relationships: Bridge between forces/Newton's_Laws (single-body) and example_2_9_n_body (chaotic many-body). Anchor in forces/N-Body_and_Chaos
identities.truth: An orbit is not a path drawn around a center — it is the trajectory two bodies negotiate when neither wants to let the other go.

identities.essence: N bodies each attracting every other — O(n²) gravitational sum, classic chaotic dynamics with no closed-form solution
identities.desire: To show that two-body solvability vanishes the moment a third body enters — chaos arrives at n=3, not n=∞
identities.critical_parameter: body count and gravitational_constant — count gates whether the system can be reasoned about; G scales how fast collapse comes
identities.triggers: Three bodies near-equal mass produce sensitive-dependence chaos; one heavy body recovers near-Keplerian orbits for the rest; high G collapses everything to a singular cluster
identities.emerges: Self-organization without design — clusters form, eject members, stabilize into binaries; Poincaré's three-body insight lived as motion
identities.needs: per-body mass [has], pairwise force computation [has], trails [has], stability tuning [has]
identities.relationships: Direct successor to example_2_8_two_body. Anchor in forces/N-Body_and_Chaos. Companion to vector_field_visualizer (field view)
identities.truth: Three bodies cannot be solved — they can only be watched. The future is a fact computed forward, not predicted from the past.

identities.essence: circle(center, r, d) = torus(r) + circle(center, r * 0.5, d-1), concentric halving
identities.desire: To introduce recursion visually — each ring half the size of the last, rainbow colors marking each depth level
identities.critical_parameter: max_depth — at 6 the innermost ring is 1/64th of the original, nearly invisible, proving the recursion continues beyond sight
identities.triggers: show_animation → rings appear one depth at a time; animation_speed controls the reveal rhythm
identities.emerges: The visual proof that halving never reaches zero — the rings keep going, each smaller but present
identities.needs: VR depth control [missing], animation toggle [has]
identities.relationships: The simplest recursion example; precedes example_8_2 (squares) and example_8_3 (branching circles)
identities.truth: Recursion is a function that trusts its smaller self to do the same work — and the concentric circles are the proof that trust was warranted.
