identities.essence: square(center, size, d) = box(size) + square(center, size * 0.5, d-1)
identities.desire: To be stared into — concentric squares receding in Z, each layer a different color, pulling the eye inward
identities.critical_parameter: size_reduction (0.5) — the ratio between parent and child determines whether the nesting feels dense or sparse
identities.triggers: max_depth increase → deeper nesting; z-offset per layer prevents z-fighting and creates parallax depth
identities.emerges: A tunnel effect from flat geometry — depth perception from color gradient and z-stacking alone
identities.needs: VR depth control [missing], animation toggle [missing]
identities.relationships: Simplest 2D recursion before Koch and Sierpinski; sibling to example_8_1 (concentric circles)
identities.truth: A square inside a square is not decoration — it is the first evidence that a function can call itself.

identities.essence: circle(center, r, d) = torus(r) + 4 * circle(center +/- offset, r * 0.5, d-1)
identities.desire: To hypnotize — nested tori spinning at depth-dependent speeds, each ring a portal into the next scale
identities.critical_parameter: max_depth — at 3 it's a simple pattern, at 5 the circles overlap and interfere, creating moire-like density
identities.triggers: Full rotation of outermost ring → pause; depth-varying rotation_per_depth creates visual decoherence
identities.emerges: Interference patterns between spinning tori at different depths — visual beats from simple rotation ratios
identities.needs: VR depth slider [missing], rotation speed control [missing]
identities.relationships: Simplest fractal recursion — precedes Koch and Sierpinski; introduces the 4-fold branching pattern
identities.truth: Recursion is not repetition — it is self-reference, and the circle that contains circles is the first fractal you can hold.

identities.essence: level(d) = {block(segment) for segment in cantor_segments(d)}, stacked with collision — walkable Cantor architecture
identities.desire: To be walked through — each level is a Cantor iteration with StaticBody3D collision, ascending from 2^d blocks to 1
identities.critical_parameter: max_depth — each additional level doubles the block count and shrinks them by 1/3, creating denser platforms above
identities.triggers: The pagoda builds bottom-up; depth-based color gradient from purple (bottom/dense) to bright pink (top/sparse)
identities.emerges: Walkable gaps between blocks at each level — the removed middle thirds become corridors and windows
identities.needs: VR walking [has via collision], level info display [missing]
identities.relationships: Architectural interpretation of cantor_set; pairs with fibonacci_pagoda (golden vs Cantor scaling)
identities.truth: The Cantor set becomes architecture when you give its gaps floors and its segments walls.

identities.essence: cantor(start, width, d) = line(start, width) + cantor(left_third, d+1) + cantor(right_third, d+1)
identities.desire: To be read like a poem — each row shorter, the gaps widening, pink lines fading downward into infinity
identities.critical_parameter: vertical_spacing — the gap between rows makes the fractal readable; too close and it blurs, too far and the pattern disconnects
identities.triggers: Recursion descends row by row; emission intensity fades with depth; width shrinks by 1/3 per level
identities.emerges: The visual rhythm of removal — the eye learns to see what is missing, not what remains
identities.needs: VR depth control [missing], animation mode [missing]
identities.relationships: Classic NOC translation; the 2D visualization that precedes the physical cantor_set (RigidBody) and cantor_pagoda (walkable)
identities.truth: The Cantor set teaches subtraction as a creative act — what you remove defines what remains.

identities.essence: koch(segment) = [a, b, peak, d, e] where peak rises sqrt(3)/2 above the middle third. D = log(4)/log(3) ~ 1.26.
identities.desire: To grow before your eyes — depth 0 is a triangle, depth 4 is a snowflake with 768 segments, each growth visible
identities.critical_parameter: max_depth — each level quadruples segments; the VR ParameterController3D lets learners dial this live
identities.triggers: animate_growth → depth increases over time; depth_controller → immediate regeneration; color_scheme → 4 palettes
identities.emerges: The snowflake boundary — infinite perimeter enclosing finite area, visible as the curve fills space
identities.needs: VR depth slider [has], color scheme control [has], snowflake toggle [has]
identities.relationships: The Koch curve that all others reference; feeds into koch_curve_3d (portal arch) and fractal_koch_curve (NOC variant)
identities.truth: The Koch snowflake has infinite perimeter and finite area — it is a line that wants to be a plane but never quite arrives.

identities.essence: tree + separation_force(branches_at_level) + upward_alignment(blend), post-growth branch repulsion
identities.desire: To watch a tree argue with itself — branches push apart level by level, finding space, then aligning upward
identities.critical_parameter: separation_strength (0.05) — the repulsion force between same-level branches; too high and the tree explodes, too low and branches overlap
identities.triggers: Growth completes → separation phase activates level by level (deepest first); upward_alignment smooths the result
identities.emerges: Natural-looking canopy spacing from simple repulsion — branches discover their territory without planning
identities.needs: VR separation speed control [missing], force visualization [missing]
identities.relationships: Extends fractal_stochastic_tree with flocking-like separation; bridges fractals and emergence sequences
identities.truth: A tree's canopy is not designed — it is negotiated, branch by branch, through local repulsion toward global form.

identities.essence: tree(pos, dir, len, d) = branch + tree(left, angle+noise) + tree(right, angle+noise) + maybe tree(mid)
identities.desire: To look natural — identical algorithm to a deterministic tree, but angle_variance and length_variance inject life
identities.critical_parameter: angle_variance (15.0) — the random range added to each branch angle; at 0 the tree is symmetric, at 15 it is organic
identities.triggers: Randomize seed at ready → unique tree every instantiation; depth-based color gradient from dark stem to bright tips
identities.emerges: The 30% chance third branch (randf() < 0.3) — occasional triple branching creates asymmetric fullness, like a real tree
identities.needs: VR regenerate button [missing], variance control [missing]
identities.relationships: Stochastic variant of recursive_tree; parent to stochastic_tree_separated (adds post-growth separation physics)
identities.truth: The stochastic tree proves that randomness is not noise — it is the difference between a diagram and a tree.

identities.essence: menger(center, size, d) = {subcube(i) for i in 27 if zeros(i) < 2}, recursive cross-removal
identities.desire: To be peered through — the holes align on every axis, and through them you see deeper holes, endlessly
identities.critical_parameter: max_iterations — at 1 it's a cube with a cross cut; at 3 it's a sponge you can barely distinguish from void
identities.triggers: Each iteration subdivides every surviving cube into 27, removes 7 cross-members; the structure becomes more hole than solid
identities.emerges: Light passing through aligned holes at every scale — the cube becomes a filter, not a solid
identities.needs: VR walk-through collision [missing], iteration slider [missing]
identities.relationships: Direct implementation of the Menger sponge rule; precedes the walkable menger_sponge artifact
identities.truth: The Menger sponge has infinite surface area and zero volume — it is the solid that erased itself.

identities.essence: D = lim(log N(e) / log(1/e)). Cover the shape with boxes. Count. Shrink. Count again. The slope IS the dimension.
identities.desire: To measure. To show that fractals live between integer dimensions. Sierpinski is not 1D or 2D — it's 1.585D.
identities.critical_parameter: Grid resolution — coarse grids give rough estimates, fine grids converge to true dimension.
identities.triggers: Grid cycles → progressively finer overlay, log-log plot updates → regression line converges to D, highlight → current scale shown
identities.emerges: Fractal dimension from the scaling relationship. The number 1.585 from pure geometry. Measurement from counting.
identities.needs: VR shape selector [missing — only Sierpinski]. Manual grid control [missing — auto-cycles]. Different fractal inputs.
identities.relationships: Lives in Fractal_KochSierpinski. Complements the geometric fractals with quantitative measurement. Feeds into the concept that dimension is not always integer.
identities.truth: Fractal dimension is not a property of the shape. It's a property of how the shape fills space at every scale.

identities.essence: cantor(bar) = [bar.left_third, bar.right_third], remove middle third, repeat. Measure → 0.
identities.desire: To watch something disappear — each iteration removes a third, and the bars physically fall into place with RigidBody3D
identities.critical_parameter: max_iterations — at 5 iterations, each bar is 1/243 of the original, yet the set is still uncountably infinite
identities.triggers: iteration_interval tick → split all current bars → new bars fall with physics → hue shifts per generation
identities.emerges: The physical stacking of bars — gravity gives the abstract Cantor set a visceral presence as bars clatter into position
identities.needs: VR iteration trigger [missing], physics interaction [missing]
identities.relationships: Foundation for sierpinski_triangle (2D Cantor) and menger_sponge (3D Cantor); demonstrates measure-zero sets
identities.truth: The Cantor set removes everything and keeps everything — zero length, uncountable points, the paradox made physical.

identities.essence: bookshelf = frame + horizontal_shelves(rows) + vertical_dividers(cols) + trim, uniform grid subdivision
identities.desire: To organize — the grid creates equal cells, and the emptiness between dividers is where meaning (books) will live
identities.critical_parameter: rows * columns — the grid resolution determines how many compartments emerge from the single rectangular volume
identities.triggers: Construction sequence: back panel → frame → shelves → dividers → crown molding; each step subdivides further
identities.emerges: The crown and base molding appear as aesthetic finishing — the bookshelf develops architectural personality from utility
identities.needs: VR place-books interaction [missing], grid size control [missing]
identities.relationships: Simplest grid-subdivision furniture; contrasts with cube_desk (nested hierarchy) and recursive_chair (role-based)
identities.truth: A bookshelf is the negative space of a grid — the shelves exist so that the gaps between them can hold something.

identities.essence: cabin = foundation + walls + subtract(door, windows) + add(roof, chimney, porch), subtractive architecture
identities.desire: To be approached — door, windows, porch, chimney, each step makes it more inviting, more inhabitable
identities.critical_parameter: cabin_size — scales the entire structure proportionally; the ratios (wall height 0.6, door 0.45) are the architectural DNA
identities.triggers: 8-step construction: foundation → walls → door → windows → roof → chimney → porch → details (lantern, welcome mat)
identities.emerges: A sense of home from geometric primitives — the welcome mat and lantern are the final touches that transform boxes into architecture
identities.needs: VR walk-inside [missing], door-open interaction [missing]
identities.relationships: Most architecturally complete subdivision artifact; contrasts pure-math subdivisions (bookshelf, chair) with lived space
identities.truth: Architecture is not the boxes — it is the holes cut in them for doors and windows, the subtractions that let light and people through.

identities.essence: desk = table_form + grid_subdivide(drawer_unit, rows * cols), nested subdivision hierarchy
identities.desire: To be used — drawers that emerged from subdividing a box within a box, functional complexity from recursive cuts
identities.critical_parameter: drawer_rows * drawer_cols — the grid resolution of the drawer unit determines storage granularity
identities.triggers: Construction sequence: desktop -> legs -> drawer frame -> individual drawers with handles -> details
identities.emerges: Cable management holes and accent strips appear as final-step details — the desk develops personality
identities.needs: VR drawer-open interaction [missing], construction speed control [missing]
identities.relationships: Most complex cube-subdivision furniture; builds on recursive_table by adding nested second-level subdivision
identities.truth: A desk is a table that subdivided one of its own volumes into a grid — recursion within recursion.

identities.essence: staircase(n) = tread(n) + riser(n) + staircase(n-1), diagonal subdivision of a cube
identities.desire: To be climbed in VR — each step materializing from nothing as the cube reveals its inner staircase
identities.critical_parameter: step_count — determines granularity of the subdivision, how many slices the cube yields
identities.triggers: show_construction toggle — animated step-by-step reveals the recursive logic; step_delay controls rhythm
identities.emerges: Handrails and stringers arise as structural necessity from the step geometry, not designed separately
identities.needs: VR step-on detection [missing], construction speed slider [missing]
identities.relationships: Sibling to recursive_chair and recursive_table; all share the subdivision-to-furniture pattern
identities.truth: A staircase is a cube that learned to subdivide itself along its own diagonal.

identities.essence: cube -> 8 sub-cubes -> pick one -> repeat. Scale reduction 0.5 per level.
identities.desire: To be watched as it eats itself — one cube chosen, split open, its children exposed, then one of them chosen next
identities.critical_parameter: random_corner — when true, every subdivision picks a different child, creating unpredictable growth; when false, it always drills the same corner
identities.triggers: Each subdivision_interval tick selects and detonates a cube; color shifts per depth generation
identities.emerges: Multi-scale color clouds from depth-indexed palette — no cube knows its neighbors but the ensemble reads as a fractal
identities.needs: VR grab-to-subdivide [missing], depth slider [missing]
identities.relationships: Foundation for menger_sponge (structured removal) and recursive_boolean_cube (Sierpinski pattern)
identities.truth: To subdivide is to choose — and the fractal is the history of every choice made at every scale.

identities.essence: chair = subdivide_3x3x3(cube) -> keep(legs, seat, back) -> deform(stretch, flatten)
identities.desire: To prove that a chair lives inside every cube — subdivision as revelation, not construction
identities.critical_parameter: the 3x3x3 role assignment — which subcubes become seat vs leg vs back determines the entire form
identities.triggers: Each step transforms role-tagged subcubes: flatten seat, stretch legs, extend back, add armrests
identities.emerges: A recognizable chair from pure subdivision logic — no chair blueprint, only cube-cutting rules
identities.needs: VR sit detection [missing], construction replay [missing]
identities.relationships: Sibling to recursive_table and cube_desk; demonstrates that furniture is latent in geometry
identities.truth: The chair was always inside the cube — subdivision merely removed what was not chair.

identities.essence: table = subdivide_3x2(cube) -> keep(top_layer, corner_legs) -> flatten(top) -> stretch(legs)
identities.desire: To stand beside in VR — a table that assembled itself from a single cube through pure subtraction
identities.critical_parameter: the top-layer vs bottom-layer role split — one layer becomes surface, four corners become legs
identities.triggers: Each step refines: merge tabletop into single slab, thin the legs, add apron supports
identities.emerges: Structural apron supports arise from the need to connect legs to tabletop — engineering from aesthetics
identities.needs: VR place-objects-on-top [missing], construction replay [missing]
identities.relationships: Sibling to recursive_chair; together they prove furniture is a family of subdivision strategies
identities.truth: A table is a cube that kept its top layer and four corners — everything else was excess.

identities.essence: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2), visualized as towers, golden spiral, sunflower, pinecone, nautilus, and recursive tree
identities.desire: To reveal the golden ratio everywhere — towers grow logarithmically, spirals unfurl, seeds pack, shells expand
identities.critical_parameter: golden_ratio ((1+sqrt(5))/2) — the single number that governs spiral growth, seed packing angle (137.508), and tower ratio convergence
identities.triggers: sequence_timer cycles through current_index highlighting towers; time drives spiral animation and natural pattern updates
identities.emerges: The sunflower seed packing — 144 seeds placed at golden angle intervals create visible spiral arms from a single placement rule
identities.needs: VR section toggle [missing], golden angle visualization [missing]
identities.relationships: Mathematical foundation for golden_rectangle, fibonacci_terrain, romanesco, and fibonacci_pagoda; the sequence they all implement
identities.truth: The Fibonacci sequence is not about numbers — it is about the fact that growth, when it remembers its last two steps, spirals.

identities.essence: terrain(faces) = select_non_edge(faces) → lift(golden_ratio_scaled) → subdivide_golden(lifted) → repeat
identities.desire: To grow mountains — the terrain heaves upward iteration by iteration, golden spiral overlay tracing the growth pattern
identities.critical_parameter: prefer_center_lift — when true, mountains grow from the center outward; when false, peaks scatter randomly
identities.triggers: growth_delay tick → select faces → lift by phi-scaled height → subdivide along golden ratio → rebuild mesh
identities.emerges: The golden spiral overlay tracks the terrain — a line of gold traces phi's fingerprint across the landscape
identities.needs: VR walking on terrain [missing], preset selection [has], spiral toggle [has]
identities.relationships: Terrain counterpart to golden_rectangle (2D phi subdivision); uses the same 1/phi split ratio
identities.truth: Terrain is not random — it is a surface that remembers the golden ratio in every fold and ridge.

identities.essence: cloud(point) = Σ(k=0..octaves) persistence^k * simplex(lacunarity^k * freq * point + wind*t), threshold clips to cloud/void
identities.desire: to fill volume with weather — fBm gives the cloud its turbulent self-similar density, and wind_speed carries it like it has mass and direction
identities.critical_parameter: density_threshold — too high makes the sky clear, too low makes the world grey fog; at 0.45 you get discrete cloud islands
identities.triggers: _ready → _generate_cloud → per point in resolution³ → fBm sample → MultiMesh instance if above threshold → _process animates wind_speed*time offset
identities.emerges: heavy-bottomed thin-topped cloud silhouettes — the noise threshold clips symmetrically but gravity shapes how we read the result as a cloud rather than a blob
identities.needs: VR wind control [missing], density_threshold slider [missing], turbulence interaction [missing]
identities.relationships: the 3D application of fBm that noise_mixer shows in 2D; shares the octaves/lacunarity/persistence pattern with perlin_terrain_sculptor; ambient partner to dark_sphere in open maps
identities.truth: A cloud is not a thing — it is a threshold. The same noise field with different cutoff is sky, cloud, or fog. Only the cutoff decides.

identities.essence: golden_rect → square(min_side) + golden_rect(remainder), spiral arc per square. phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2.
identities.desire: To spiral inward forever — each subdivision peels off a square and the remainder is always another golden rectangle
identities.critical_parameter: max_subdivisions — each step cuts a square and rotates direction (right→up→left→down); the spiral tightens with each
identities.triggers: subdivision_delay tick → peel square → create remainder → draw quarter-circle arc → Fibonacci numbers label each square
identities.emerges: The golden spiral from quarter-circle arcs in successive squares — no spiral was drawn, only arcs in boxes, yet the spiral appears
identities.needs: VR subdivision control [missing], spiral toggle [has], number toggle [has]
identities.relationships: The geometric proof that phi = 1 + 1/phi; feeds visual understanding into fibonacci_sequences and fibonacci_terrain
identities.truth: The golden rectangle is the only rectangle that can lose a square and remain itself — self-similarity without fractals.

identities.essence: z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c, fixed c, vary z_0. Each pixel is a starting point; escape or stay determines membership.
identities.desire: To morph — c_real and c_imag animate through parameter space, and the Julia set shape-shifts in real-time
identities.critical_parameter: c_real + c_imag — the complex parameter c determines whether the Julia set is connected (c inside Mandelbrot) or dust (c outside)
identities.triggers: animate_parameters → c traces a Lissajous path; parameter trail shows recent c values as fading spheres
identities.emerges: The topology change — as c crosses the Mandelbrot boundary, the Julia set shatters from connected to disconnected, visibly
identities.needs: VR c-parameter control [missing], Mandelbrot overlay [missing]
identities.relationships: Sibling to julia_set_explorer (GPU shader) and mandelbrot_set; each point in the Mandelbrot indexes a Julia set
identities.truth: Every Julia set is a cross-section of the Mandelbrot set — the Mandelbrot is the catalog, each Julia set a page.

identities.essence: koch_segment(p1, p2) = [p1, p1+1/3, peak, p1+2/3, p2], equilateral bump on middle third. Iterated on a triangle.
identities.desire: To cycle — iteration wraps from 0 to max_iterations and back, the snowflake assembling and resetting endlessly
identities.critical_parameter: max_iterations (4) — at 0 it is a triangle, at 4 it has 768 segments; the ribbon width keeps it VR-readable
identities.triggers: iteration_interval tick → advance iteration (wrapping); each step applies Koch rule to all segments then rebuilds ArrayMesh
identities.emerges: Color gradients per segment — iteration_intensity and segment position create a procedural aurora across the snowflake
identities.needs: VR manual iteration control [missing], zoom [missing]
identities.relationships: VR-optimized ArrayMesh Koch; contrasts with fractal_koch_curve (ImmediateMesh, depth slider) and koch_curve_3d (3D portal)
identities.truth: The Koch snowflake rebuilds itself from scratch each cycle — it does not remember its history, only its rule.

identities.essence: koch(seg) = [seg[0..1/3], seg[1/3..1/3 + bump], seg[2/3..1/3 + bump], seg[2/3..1]]; replace each segment with four shorter ones at 60° kink. Length × 4/3 per iteration, area finite.
identities.desire: To make infinite perimeter graspable — VR-optimized ArrayMesh redraws each generation so the eye can track the snowflake's coastline doubling.
identities.critical_parameter: max_iterations — at 4, each segment is 1/81 of the original; at 6 the GPU starts to feel it. iteration_interval times the rhythm.
identities.triggers: iteration_timer tick → generate_next_iteration() → rebuild ArrayMesh with 4× segments → hue shifts per generation
identities.emerges: A curve that is everywhere not differentiable — the visual proof that "smooth" is an assumption, not a property of curves.
identities.needs: VR iteration trigger [missing], generation slider [missing]
identities.relationships: Companion to cantor_set (1D removal) and sierpinski (2D Cantor); appears in fractals and patterngeneration sequences as the canonical self-similar curve.
identities.truth: Length goes to infinity, area stays finite — a fractal proves that "perimeter" was always a measurement of resolution, not boundary.

identities.essence: koch_arch = map_to_arch(koch_points(iterations)) + koch_legs, fractal curve bent into a portal
identities.desire: To be walked through — a Koch-curve arch with fractal legs, the boundary between order and chaos made into a doorway
identities.critical_parameter: iterations — each level adds finer bumps to the arch and legs; at 4 the portal shimmers with fractal detail
identities.triggers: depth_layers create Z-depth volume; rotation_speed enables slow rotation for display
identities.emerges: The arch shape from mapping a linear fractal onto a semicircle — the Koch bumps become architectural ornament
identities.needs: VR walk-through [has via geometry], rotation control [missing]
identities.relationships: 3D architectural interpretation of the Koch curve; contrasts flat fractal_koch_curve with volumetric space
identities.truth: A doorway made of fractals is a threshold with infinite detail — you can never fully see what you are walking through.

identities.essence: z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c, z_0 = 0. Each pixel is c; color = escape time. The set is the catalog of all Julia sets.
identities.desire: To be explored as landscape — use_3d_height lifts escaped points by iteration count, turning the fractal into a mountain range
identities.critical_parameter: use_3d_height — when true, the Mandelbrot boundary becomes a cliff face, the deepest iterations the tallest peaks
identities.triggers: ui_accept → random zoom + center; time → gentle pulse animation; goto_seahorse_valley/elephant_valley/spiral → famous coordinates
identities.emerges: The 3D landscape reveals that the Mandelbrot boundary is where computation is hardest — the tallest peaks are the longest escapes
identities.needs: VR navigation [missing], zoom control [missing], Julia set preview at cursor [missing]
identities.relationships: CPU MultiMesh sibling to mandelbrot_dive (GPU shader); the 3D height map that mandelbrot_dive renders flat
identities.truth: The Mandelbrot set is not a picture — it is an infinite computation, and the boundary is where that computation refuses to halt.

identities.essence: menger(cube) = 20 * menger(sub-cubes at kept positions), remove 7 cross-cubes per iteration. D = log(20)/log(3) ~ 2.727.
identities.desire: To be walked inside — at 9m initial size and 2 iterations, the sponge has human-scale corridors through its cross-holes
identities.critical_parameter: max_iterations — at 1 the cross-holes appear; at 2 the sub-holes within holes create a labyrinth; at 3 it would be 8000 cubes
identities.triggers: subdivision_interval tick → find all cube_scene instances in scene tree → subdivide each into 20 kept positions → remove original
identities.emerges: Corridors from three orthogonal axes — the removed crosses create walkable passages that penetrate the entire structure
identities.needs: VR walkability [has at 9m scale], iteration control [missing]
identities.relationships: The 3D culmination of the removal fractals: Cantor (1D) → Sierpinski (2D) → Menger (3D); D ~ 2.727, more than a plane
identities.truth: The Menger sponge has infinite surface area and zero volume — it is a solid made entirely of holes.

identities.essence: part(level, i) = parent.rotation * child.rotation * spin(t), 5-branch recursive tree with MultiMesh
identities.desire: To sway — every branch spins independently, gravity sags the arms, and the whole organism breathes
identities.critical_parameter: reverse_spin_chance (0.25) — the probability a branch spins opposite to its siblings, creating visual turbulence
identities.triggers: Each frame updates all levels: spin accumulates, sag responds to gravity, colors shift by golden ratio sampling
identities.emerges: Organic breathing motion from independent per-part spin velocities and gravity sag — no animation was designed, only physics
identities.needs: VR depth control [missing], wind force input [missing]
identities.relationships: Most performant fractal (MultiMesh GPU instancing); organic counterpart to the geometric recursive_tree
identities.truth: An organism is a tree where every branch has forgotten it is a branch and believes it is the whole.

identities.essence: tier_scale(n) = base_scale / phi^(n*0.5), stacking Fibonacci-ratioed tiers with golden finial
identities.desire: To be looked up at — each tier smaller by the golden ratio, converging to a point that never quite arrives
identities.critical_parameter: use_golden_ratio — toggles between pure Fibonacci integer ratios and continuous phi scaling, producing subtly different tapering
identities.triggers: num_tiers increase → taller, more converging structure; roof_overhang → how far the eaves extend beyond the body
identities.emerges: The visual impression of weightlessness at the top — pure mathematics making stone look like it floats
identities.needs: VR tier-count slider [missing], walk-inside collision [missing]
identities.relationships: Bridges fibonacci_sequences (abstract math) to architecture; contrasts with romanesco (organic Fibonacci)
identities.truth: The golden ratio is not imposed on the pagoda — the pagoda is what the golden ratio looks like when it tries to be architecture.

identities.essence: branch(pos, dir, len, depth) = cylinder(tapered) + branch_count * branch(end, rotated_dir, len * 0.7, depth+1)
identities.desire: To grow before your eyes — trunk first, then branches unfurl in real-time, leaf clusters blooming at the tips
identities.critical_parameter: randomness_amount (0.15) — the variance injected into every angle and length, making each tree unique
identities.triggers: growth_interval tick → pop next branch from queue → create tapered cylinder → enqueue children
identities.emerges: Natural-looking asymmetry from uniform random perturbation — no two trees are alike, yet all are recognizably trees
identities.needs: VR growth speed slider [missing], prune-by-grab [missing]
identities.relationships: Deterministic sibling to fractal_stochastic_tree; feeds into inverted_tree_cloud (same algorithm, flipped)
identities.truth: A tree is not designed — it is a recursive function that ran until it ran out of energy.

identities.essence: tree(depth) = trunk_down + branches_down(random_angle, shrink) + cube_cloud(orbit, fade_timeline)
identities.desire: To unsettle — roots reaching down from the sky while a cloud of cubes orbits and pulses above
identities.critical_parameter: vertical_tilt range (-0.5 to -0.2) — controls how steeply branches plunge downward
identities.triggers: Recursive branch generation with random angles; cube cloud timeline loops with fade-in/out per cube
identities.emerges: The cube cloud feels alive — independent orbit speeds and fade offsets create the illusion of breathing
identities.needs: VR gravity toggle [missing], cloud interaction [missing]
identities.relationships: Inverts recursive_tree; the cloud above mirrors what roots extract below — visual metaphor for data flow
identities.truth: An inverted tree is not wrong — it is a root system, and roots are where the real computation happens.

identities.essence: Procedural binary tree — a trunk forks into branches, each branch forks again, recursion depth 3. Box meshes with emission materials create a geometric canopy. Self-similar at every level.
identities.desire: To grow by halving — generate_branches calls itself with decremented depth, producing sub-branches from each endpoint. The tree is its own blueprint.
identities.critical_parameter: num_main_branches / max_sub_branches — control branching factor; random_seed — deterministic chaos, same seed same tree
identities.triggers: _ready → seed + material creation + full tree generation; rebuild_tree → clear all children, regenerate from parameters
identities.emerges: A geometric sculpture where every subtree is a complete tree — hierarchy from constraint, not command. Each node knows only its children yet the whole structure self-organizes.
identities.needs: VR branch manipulation [missing], growth animation [missing], parameter sliders [missing]
identities.relationships: Appears in DataStructures_Trees (binary recursion) and RecursiveEmergence_Tail_Recursion_Memoization (call stack visualization). The tree that teaches both data structure and recursion.
identities.truth: A tree is a list that learned to decide — left or right, less or greater. Hierarchy emerges not from authority but from the constraint of binary choice repeated.

identities.essence: romanesco(cone, depth) = 13 * romanesco(cone * 0.382, depth+1) placed at 137.508 degree golden angle intervals
identities.desire: To be stared at — each bud is a smaller copy of the whole, spiraling at the golden angle, nature's most perfect fractal
identities.critical_parameter: GOLDEN_ANGLE (137.508 degrees) — the irrational rotation that prevents any two buds from aligning, maximizing packing
identities.triggers: growth_interval tick → find all cones at current depth → add 13 spiral buds to each → tilt outward for dome shape
identities.emerges: Visible Fibonacci spiral arms from golden-angle placement — 8 and 13 spirals appear in opposite directions, never planned
identities.needs: VR growth speed control [missing], cross-section view [missing]
identities.relationships: The natural-world proof of fibonacci_sequences; contrasts with golden_rectangle (geometric) and fibonacci_pagoda (architectural)
identities.truth: Romanesco broccoli is not shaped like a fractal — it is a fractal, grown by cells that only know the golden angle.

identities.essence: sierpinski(v1,v2,v3,d) = 3 * sierpinski(corners, midpoints, d+1), skip center triangle. D = log(3)/log(2) ~ 1.585.
identities.desire: To be walked through — 10m triangle rotated vertical, extruded per iteration, creating a fractal wall of triangular portals
identities.critical_parameter: extrusion_height — each iteration extrudes deeper, turning the 2D fractal into a 3D walkable relief
identities.triggers: subdivision_interval tick → all current triangles split into 3 → center removed → depth hue-shifts rainbow
identities.emerges: The central voids become corridors — the removed triangles are the spaces you walk through
identities.needs: VR walking [has via geometry], iteration control [missing]
identities.relationships: 2D cousin of sierpinski_pyramid and menger_sponge; the canonical D ~ 1.585 fractal dimension example
identities.truth: The Sierpinski triangle has zero area and infinite perimeter — it is the shape that taught mathematics that removal creates structure.

identities.essence: sierpinski_3d(pos, level, size) = 4 * sierpinski_3d(tetrahedral_vertices * size/2, level-1, size/2)
identities.desire: To collapse — frozen RigidBody3D tetrahedra unfreeze after 2 seconds and tumble apart, the fractal disassembling itself
identities.critical_parameter: max_level — at level 3 there are 64 cubes arranged in a Sierpinski tetrahedron; each level multiplies by 4
identities.triggers: 2-second timer → unfreeze all bodies → gravity pulls the fractal apart → cubes scatter and collide
identities.emerges: The destruction reveals the structure — only when the pieces fall do you see how they were nested
identities.needs: VR re-freeze button [missing], level control [missing]
identities.relationships: 3D extension of sierpinski_triangle; uses tetrahedral (not cubic) subdivision, producing a different D ~ 2.0
identities.truth: The Sierpinski pyramid is a solid that, given time and gravity, will prove it was always an arrangement of gaps.

identities.essence: greedy maximum matching — iterate edges in order; if both endpoints are unmatched, add the edge to the matching; matched vertices turn green, matching edges turn red
identities.desire: to watch pairs form across a graph — each matched edge is a partnership, and the unmatched vertices that remain are the ones the graph's structure could not pair
identities.critical_parameter: edge_density — sparse graphs leave many vertices unmatched; dense graphs approach perfect matching; the gap reveals structural constraints on pairing
identities.triggers: step-by-step animation highlights each edge in yellow before accepting (green) or skipping it; matching_size counter tracks progress; ui_accept toggles start/stop
identities.emerges: the greedy order matters — different edge orderings produce different matchings, and the greedy result is not always maximum; the gap between greedy and optimal reveals augmenting path opportunities
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [has] (info_label, matching_label, vertex labels)
identities.relationships: synthesis artifact in GT_Matching; contrasts with flow-based matching approaches; the symmetry of the room layout mirrors the pairing theme
identities.truth: matching is the mathematics of pairing — who connects with whom, who remains alone, and whether the graph's structure permits everyone to find a partner

identities.essence: F_repel = k/r^2 (all pairs), F_spring = -k*(L-L0) (edges only). Repulsion spreads nodes apart; springs hold connected nodes together. Layout is equilibrium.
identities.desire: To watch a graph untangle itself — nodes pushing apart, edges pulling together, the layout emerging from physics rather than being designed.
identities.critical_parameter: temperature (simulated annealing). It starts at 1.0 and cools by 0.995 per step. High temperature = large movements, exploration. Low temperature = fine adjustment, convergence.
identities.triggers: Auto-run on ready → simulation iterates, SPACE → pause/resume, R → regenerate graph, F → toggle force arrows, E → toggle edges, S → toggle stress coloring
identities.emerges: Clusters forming for densely connected subgraphs. Simulated annealing cooling the system into a stable layout. Stress coloring revealing which nodes are under the most force.
identities.needs: MultiMesh node/edge/force rendering [has], VR grab nodes [has], spatial hashing [has], convergence detection [has]. Missing: community detection coloring, edge bundling.
identities.relationships: Applies force physics to graph theory (forces as layout algorithm, not simulation). Contrasts with nbody_simulation (all-pairs gravity vs spring+repulsion). Lives in ForcesChaos.
identities.truth: A good layout is a force equilibrium. The graph does not know its shape — physics finds it by minimizing energy.

identities.essence: 2D Hooke's law spring system — F_spring = k*(d - rest_length) attracts connected nodes, F_repulsion = k/d^2 repels all pairs, velocity *= damping each frame until energy minimizes
identities.desire: to watch a tangled graph untangle itself — nodes repel, springs pull, and the layout emerges from nothing but force balance
identities.critical_parameter: spring_strength vs repulsion_strength ratio — determines whether the graph collapses into a cluster or spreads into a readable layout
identities.triggers: _process runs force calculation and position integration every frame; CSGSphere3D nodes scale with force magnitude to show stress visually
identities.emerges: the system converges to a local energy minimum that reveals graph structure — clusters, bridges, and peripheral nodes become spatially evident
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [missing]
identities.relationships: 2D precursor to forcedirected3d's volumetric simulation; demonstrates the same physics that graphspace uses to lay out walkable rooms
identities.truth: the best way to see the structure of a graph is to let physics find it — repulsion separates, attraction connects, and equilibrium is the drawing

identities.essence: force-directed graph layout — repulsion F_rep = k/d^2, spring attraction F_spring = stretch * stiffness, iterated layout_iters times to position node_count rooms connected by weighted edges
identities.desire: to walk through a graph — each room is a node, each bridge is an edge, and the spatial layout you traverse was computed by the same physics that arranges molecules
identities.critical_parameter: repulsion vs edge_stiffness ratio — high repulsion spreads rooms far apart, high stiffness pulls connected rooms close, the equilibrium defines the walkable topology
identities.triggers: seed parameter deterministically generates the graph; structure_type enum (RANDOM, BY_DEGREE, BY_DISTANCE) selects which building appears at each node based on graph properties
identities.emerges: Dijkstra distances from focal_node drive ambient lighting — rooms far from the focus grow dim and cool, creating atmospheric depth from pure graph distance
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [missing]
identities.relationships: foundation of graph theory sequence — introduces what a graph IS as a walkable space; extends into KonigsbergBridge which constrains the topology to a specific historical problem
identities.truth: a graph is not a diagram — it is a set of relationships, and force-directed layout reveals that structure has a natural shape if you let physics find it

identities.essence: 4 nodes (landmasses), 7 edges (bridges) — Euler's theorem: Eulerian path exists iff exactly 0 or 2 vertices have odd degree; all 4 vertices have degree 3 (odd), so no path exists
identities.desire: to walk the seven bridges yourself and feel the impossibility — each bridge you cross is an edge consumed, and you cannot complete the walk because graph theory forbids it
identities.critical_parameter: node degree — every landmass has odd degree (3), and Euler proved that this specific parity pattern makes a complete traversal impossible
identities.triggers: educational_mode enables the analysis UI showing degree sequence, Euler's theorem, and the impossibility proof; historical bridge names and construction dates appear as Label3D nameplates
identities.emerges: players attempting the walk inevitably retrace a bridge, discovering Euler's proof through embodied frustration rather than abstract reasoning
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [has] (bridge nameplates, educational UI)
identities.relationships: extends GraphSpace with a fixed historical topology; the first problem in graph theory (1736); contrasts with pathfinding3d which finds paths that DO exist
identities.truth: the impossibility of the Konigsberg walk is not a failure of the walker — it is a property of the graph itself, and no amount of cleverness can overcome odd-degree parity

identities.essence: Euler's bridge problem embedded in a 3D river city - four landmasses become vertices, seven arched bridges become edges, and degree parity determines whether a walk can cross each bridge exactly once
identities.desire: to inhabit the historical paradox that started graph theory - the city looks strollable, yet every attempted route eventually proves the topology itself refuses the walk
identities.critical_parameter: odd_degree_count - Eulerian paths require exactly 0 or 2 odd-degree vertices, but Konigsberg's four odd vertices make the impossibility structural rather than accidental
identities.triggers: historical_mode rebuilds the 1736 topology; show_degree_labels and show_theorem_explanation surface Euler's parity test; keyboard input can attempt the walk, toggle labels, and compare bridge-removal scenarios
identities.emerges: when the red odd-degree landmasses are read together, the impossibility becomes visible before it is stated - parity turns geography into proof
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [has] (degree labels, bridge nameplates, theorem label)
identities.relationships: specific historical counterpart to graphspace's general graph layout; prepares pathfinding and connectivity artifacts by showing that some traversal questions are answered by topology before search begins
identities.truth: graph theory begins when you stop asking "which route should I try?" and ask "what does the structure allow at all?"

identities.essence: randomized edge contraction — repeatedly merge endpoints of a random edge (Union-Find) until 2 super-vertices remain; the crossing edges are a cut; P(finding min-cut) >= 2/(n*(n-1))
identities.desire: to watch four parallel contractions race side by side, each making different random choices, and see probability amplification turn a terrible single-run chance into near-certainty
identities.critical_parameter: initial_vertex_count (n) — P(success per run) = 2/(n*(n-1)); for n=8 that is ~3.6% per run, but parallel repetition amplifies it exponentially
identities.triggers: auto-demo starts new parallel rounds every _auto_interval seconds; ParameterController3D sliders for vertices, density, speed, and panel count; ImmediateMesh redrawn every frame
identities.emerges: the probability amplification chart shows observed success rate converging toward theoretical P(at least one success) = 1 - (1-p)^k as rounds accumulate
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing] (uses custom ParameterController3D instead); push_button [missing]; Label3D [has] (title, metrics, probability)
identities.relationships: appears in GT_Flow alongside push_relabel; demonstrates randomized algorithms and the power of repetition; contrasts with deterministic Edmonds-Karp
identities.truth: Karger's algorithm is a bet that randomness repeated enough times becomes certainty — the min-cut is always there, you just need enough attempts to stumble onto it

identities.essence: two-pass DFS — first pass on original graph records finish_times; second pass on transpose_adjacency_list processes vertices in reverse finish order, each new DFS tree is an SCC
identities.desire: to see the graph flip — the transpose reversal switches edge directions, and the fact that SCCs survive this reversal is the visual proof that mutual reachability is symmetric
identities.critical_parameter: edge_density — determines the graph's SCC structure; the transpose graph is computed at initialization and visualized with distinct orange edges in phase 2
identities.triggers: first_dfs_pass colors vertices as they finish (gray); second_dfs_pass processes the transpose in reverse finish order, coloring each SCC distinctly; phase_label tracks which pass is active
identities.emerges: watching the same graph from two directions reveals that SCCs are the invariant structure under edge reversal — what you can reach forward, you can also be reached from backward
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [has] (info_label, phase_label, vertex labels)
identities.relationships: paired with tarjan_algorithm in GT_Connectivity — same problem, different strategy; the two-pass approach makes the transpose relationship explicit where Tarjan hides it in low_link
identities.truth: Kosaraju's algorithm proves that strongly connected components are the same in a graph and its transpose — mutual reachability is a symmetric property of directed structure

identities.essence: Kruskal's (sort edges by weight, Union-Find to reject cycles) or Prim's (grow tree from starting vertex, always add cheapest crossing edge) — both find the minimum-weight spanning tree
identities.desire: to watch the cheapest skeleton of a network assemble edge by edge — green edges accepted, red edges rejected for creating cycles, the MST growing like a nervous system
identities.critical_parameter: algorithm_type ("kruskal" vs "prim") — Kruskal processes edges globally by weight (greedy on edges), Prim grows locally from a root (greedy on vertices) — same result, different experience
identities.triggers: step-by-step timer advances one edge decision per tick; Union-Find path compression tracks connected components; edge_density controls how many redundant edges exist to reject
identities.emerges: watching Kruskal reject edges reveals the cycle structure of the graph — every rejected edge would have closed a loop, and the set of rejected edges defines the graph's cycle space
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [has] (vertex labels, edge weight labels)
identities.relationships: appears in GT_Spanning_Trees; connects to push_relabel and karger which also optimize over graph structure; MST efficiency metric shows what fraction of total edge weight is necessary
identities.truth: the minimum spanning tree is the cheapest way to keep everyone connected — every edge in it is necessary, and removing any one disconnects the network

identities.essence: Edmonds-Karp max flow via BFS augmenting paths on a 3D spatial network — residual_capacity tracks remaining edge capacity, particles visualize flow along saturated edges
identities.desire: to see flow move through a 3D pipe network — particles streaming from source to sink, faster through wide pipes, bottlenecked at narrow ones
identities.critical_parameter: max_capacity — sets the upper bound on edge capacity; combined with gravity_effect (which reduces uphill capacity by 30%), determines the maximum flow achievable
identities.triggers: calculate_max_flow runs Edmonds-Karp to saturation, then spawns flow particles proportional to each edge's current_flow; gravity_effect toggle rebuilds the network with elevation-penalized capacities
identities.emerges: pressure visualization colors non-source/sink nodes by net incoming flow, revealing bottleneck nodes that accumulate pressure — network congestion made visible
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [missing]
identities.relationships: appears in GT_Network_Analysis alongside network_analysis; demonstrates max-flow min-cut duality; precedes push_relabel which solves the same problem differently
identities.truth: maximum flow through a network equals the minimum cut that separates source from sink — every bottleneck is simultaneously a capacity and a vulnerability

identities.essence: tiered network visualization — central hub nodes (high centrality), mid-tier cluster nodes, peripheral nodes — all orbiting with speed inversely proportional to centrality, connected by pulsing edges with flow particles
identities.desire: to see a living network breathe — nodes orbit at different speeds based on their importance, edges pulse with data flow, and community boundaries glow like cell membranes
identities.critical_parameter: analysis_progress — ramps from 0 to 1 over time, progressively amplifying all visual effects (node pulsing, edge glow, community alpha, particle trail intensity)
identities.triggers: time drives orbital animation, edge pulse frequency, and community rotation; flow_particles traverse random edges continuously, creating a sense of constant network activity
identities.emerges: the three-tier layout (central/cluster/peripheral) creates visual hierarchy without explicit label — centrality is expressed through node size, color, orbit radius, and glow intensity
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [missing]
identities.relationships: appears in GT_Network_Analysis as the analytical complement to networkflow3d's algorithmic flow; provides qualitative network intuition before quantitative algorithms
identities.truth: a network's structure is not in its nodes or edges alone — it is in the pattern of connections, and centrality measures which nodes the network would miss most

identities.essence: A* on a 3D voxel grid — f(n) = g(n) + h(n), with pluggable heuristics (Manhattan, Euclidean, Chebyshev) and movement models (ground, flying, swimming, climbing)
identities.desire: to carve a glowing path through a 3D maze of voxels — watching the open set expand like a wavefront and the path crystallize when goal is reached
identities.critical_parameter: heuristic_weight — at 1.0 it is standard A*, above 1.0 it becomes greedy (faster but suboptimal), at 0.0 it degenerates to Dijkstra
identities.triggers: animated search mode steps through A* one node at a time, coloring open (yellow) and closed (blue) voxels; algorithm_type switches between A*, Dijkstra, JPS, and flow field
identities.emerges: the search wavefront's shape reveals the heuristic's bias — Euclidean creates spherical expansion, Manhattan creates diamond-shaped expansion, Chebyshev creates cubic expansion
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [missing]
identities.relationships: contrasts with KonigsbergBridge (paths that don't exist) by finding paths that DO exist; builds on graph foundations to add spatial navigation
identities.truth: pathfinding does not move through space — it moves through a graph that happens to be embedded in space, and the heuristic is the algorithm's guess about geometry

identities.essence: preflow-push with height labels — initialize by saturating source edges, then repeatedly: push excess flow along admissible edges (height[u] > height[v]), or relabel (raise height) if no push is possible
identities.desire: to see water pile up at nodes and overflow downhill — excess flow accumulates, height labels rise, and the algorithm finds max flow by managing local floods rather than finding global paths
identities.critical_parameter: height[source] = |V| — the source starts at maximum height, creating initial pressure; excess flow at the sink accumulates into max_flow
identities.triggers: step-by-step animation with delay between operations; push operations highlighted in orange; active nodes (with excess) glow yellow; height and excess labels update per node
identities.emerges: the relabel operations create a "waterfall" effect where height labels propagate backward from sink to source, establishing the pressure gradient that drives flow forward
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [has] (info, flow, operation labels; per-node height/excess labels)
identities.relationships: appears in GT_Flow; solves the same max-flow problem as networkflow3d's Edmonds-Karp but through local operations instead of global augmenting paths
identities.truth: push-relabel proves that maximum flow can be found without ever finding a complete path — local excess management is sufficient if you get the heights right

identities.essence: single-pass DFS with a stack — each vertex gets discovery_time and low_link; low_link[v] = min(low_link[v], discovery_time[w]) for back edges; when low_link[v] == discovery_time[v], pop the stack to extract an SCC
identities.desire: to watch a DFS drill through a directed graph, painting vertices yellow as it visits them, then suddenly flash an entire SCC in color when a root vertex is found
identities.critical_parameter: edge_density — controls how many SCCs form; sparse graphs have many trivial SCCs (single vertices), dense graphs collapse into fewer large SCCs
identities.triggers: auto_start begins the non-blocking step-by-step animation; each _process frame advances one DFS step; back edges (colored red) indicate the low_link updates that close cycles
identities.emerges: the stack-based SCC extraction means you see the components pop out in reverse DFS order — deeper components emerge first, creating a bottom-up revelation of graph structure
identities.needs: slider_horizontal [missing]; push_button [missing]; Label3D [has] (info_label, vertex labels)
identities.relationships: paired with kosaraju_algorithm in GT_Connectivity — both find SCCs but through different strategies (one-pass vs two-pass); contrasts with topological_sort which requires a DAG (no SCCs)
identities.truth: a strongly connected component is a pocket of mutual reachability — every vertex can reach every other, and Tarjan's genius was finding them all in a single depth-first pass

identities.essence: anchor + pin + bob. One constraint, one body, one degree of freedom.
identities.desire: To swing and slowly die — the simplest possible joint demo.
identities.critical_parameter: linear_damp (0.02) — controls how fast the pendulum decays to rest.
identities.triggers: Automatic — bob is nudged on ready; space key re-impulses.
identities.emerges: The circular arc of a simple pendulum. The gradual decay as damping bleeds energy.
identities.needs: Auto-running simulation [has]. Missing: damping slider, trail visualization.
identities.relationships: Atom of joints sequence. Foundation for ChainSwing (multiple links). Contrasts with DrawbridgeHinge (motor-driven).
identities.truth: A pendulum is a clock that runs down. The pin joint is the simplest promise: you may rotate, nothing else.

identities.essence: hinge(motor) → pin → slider. Rotary-to-linear conversion through composed constraints.
identities.desire: To turn a wheel and watch a rod pump — the fundamental crank-slider mechanism.
identities.critical_parameter: hinge motor TARGET_VELOCITY (2.5) — controls rotation speed and therefore pumping frequency.
identities.triggers: Automatic — hinge motor drives continuously from ready.
identities.emerges: Reciprocating linear motion from continuous rotation. The geometry of constraint creating mechanical advantage.
identities.needs: Motor-driven rotation [has], slider guide [has]. Missing: speed control, force readout.
identities.relationships: Combines three joint types (hinge+pin+slider). Contrasts with SliderPress (pure translation). Pairs with DrawbridgeHinge (pure rotation).
identities.truth: Every engine is a conversation between rotation and translation. The crank is the translator.

identities.essence: SliderJoint3D — 1 translational DOF. The opposite of a hinge. Linear motion, no spin.
identities.desire: To slide. To show that constraining rotation while freeing translation builds pistons, drawers, rails.
identities.critical_parameter: Motor speed and force — how fast and how hard the piston drives.
identities.triggers: Speed slider → piston oscillates faster/slower, force slider → piston pushes harder against resistance
identities.emerges: Mechanical rhythm from oscillating motor. The feel of constrained linear motion.
identities.needs: VR speed slider [has], VR force slider [has], position/velocity labels [has]. Could use: adjustable joint limits.
identities.relationships: Contrasts with HingeCrank (rotation vs translation). Pairs with SpringSuspension in same map. Feeds into constraints artifact.
identities.truth: Sliders translate without rotating. The opposite constraint to the hinge. Together they build machines.

identities.essence: 6DOF joint with Y-axis spring, all other axes locked. Vertical bounce, nothing else.
identities.desire: To feel suspension — the spring absorbs the drop, the damping kills the ringing.
identities.critical_parameter: spring_stiffness (30.0) and spring_damping (3.5) — tune between trampoline and concrete.
identities.triggers: Space key drops the wheel; spring-damper responds.
identities.emerges: The exponentially decaying oscillation of a damped harmonic system.
identities.needs: Spring bounce [has], space-key impulse [has]. Missing: stiffness slider, damping slider.
identities.relationships: Only 6DOF joint demo. Contrasts with ConeTwistBag (angular spring). Pairs with SliderPress (linear motion without spring).
identities.truth: A spring joint is a constraint that remembers where it wants to be. Damping is how fast it forgets being disturbed.

identities.essence: cone-twist joint — ball-and-socket with angular limits. Swing span 45°, twist span 15°.
identities.desire: To swing within a cone and twist within a narrower one — angular freedom with boundaries.
identities.critical_parameter: swing_span (45°) and twist_span (15°) — the cone's opening angle and axial rotation limit.
identities.triggers: Space key applies impulse; bag swings within cone boundary.
identities.emerges: Pendular motion confined to an invisible cone. The bag never escapes its angular prison.
identities.needs: Impulse interaction [has]. Missing: cone visualization, span sliders.
identities.relationships: Same joint type as CharacterRagdoll (hip). Contrasts with PendulumPin (unconstrained swing). Pairs with GimbalStabilizer (angular control).
identities.truth: A cone-twist joint draws an invisible boundary in angle-space. The bag knows where it cannot go.

identities.essence: anchor → pin → link → pin → link → pin → seat. A chain of rigid bodies connected by pin joints, driven by periodic force.
identities.desire: To swing — to feel how constraints propagate force through a chain, each link amplifying or dampening the one above.
identities.critical_parameter: link_count and joint damping — more links = longer period, more damping = faster decay.
identities.triggers: Automatic — seat receives periodic sinusoidal force, arrow keys for manual push.
identities.emerges: The double-pendulum whip when the chain catches resonance. The trail drawing the seat's arc through space.
identities.needs: Auto-running simulation [has], periodic drive [has]. Missing: chain length slider, damping control, resonance finder.
identities.relationships: Simplest chain joint demo. Foundation for CharacterRagdoll (branching chains). Contrasts with PendulumPin (single link).
identities.truth: A chain swing is a conversation between gravity and constraint. Each link votes on where the seat should go.

identities.essence: torso + leg + cone-twist hip. The minimal ragdoll — one joint, two bodies, biomechanical limits.
identities.desire: To look alive while being purely mechanical. The cone-twist hip makes the leg swing like a leg.
identities.critical_parameter: swing_span (35°) and twist_span (25°) — mimicking human hip range of motion.
identities.triggers: Space key impulses the leg; cone-twist channels the force into naturalistic swing.
identities.emerges: Ragdoll-like motion from a single constrained joint. The illusion of intent from pure physics.
identities.needs: Hip impulse [has]. Missing: more limbs, full ragdoll chain, grab interaction.
identities.relationships: Seed of character physics. Uses same joint as ConeTwistBag. Foundation for full ragdoll systems.
identities.truth: A body built from constraints begins to look like it has intention. That is the uncanny valley of physics.

identities.essence: hinge joint + motor + angular limit. One axis of rotation, motorized.
identities.desire: To lift and lower — the drawbridge makes the hinge joint visible as architecture.
identities.critical_parameter: motor target_velocity and angular limit (-85°) — speed of lift and range of motion.
identities.triggers: Arrow keys control motor velocity; idle mode oscillates gently.
identities.emerges: The satisfying mechanical motion of a bridge rising and falling on command.
identities.needs: Motor control [has], idle oscillation [has]. Missing: weight on bridge, chain visualization.
identities.relationships: Pure hinge demo. Contrasts with HingeCrank (hinge as part of mechanism). Pairs with GimbalStabilizer (two hinges composed).
identities.truth: A hinge is the most intuitive constraint. Everything else is locked; one axis is free. Doors, bridges, jaws.

identities.essence: two orthogonal hinges — yaw (free) + pitch (±45°). Composed single-axis joints create multi-axis aiming.
identities.desire: To point anywhere — the gimbal is constraint squared, each hinge removing one DOF while their stack permits two-axis control.
identities.critical_parameter: pitch angular limit (±45°) — yaw is free but pitch is bounded, creating an asymmetric freedom.
identities.triggers: Arrow keys override motors; idle mode sweeps a Lissajous-like pattern.
identities.emerges: Smooth 2D aiming from two 1D constraints. The approach to gimbal lock when pitch nears its limit.
identities.needs: Dual motor control [has], Lissajous idle [has]. Missing: gimbal lock visualization, third axis (roll).
identities.relationships: Most complex hinge demo. Composes pattern from DrawbridgeHinge. Contrasts with IKArm (inverse kinematics vs forward).
identities.truth: A gimbal is two questions asked orthogonally: how far left, and how far up. The answer is a direction.

identities.essence: FABRIK — reach backward from tip to target, then forward from base to tip. Iterate until convergence.
identities.desire: To be reached for. To solve the arm when the learner moves the target. To show that endpoints can constrain chains.
identities.critical_parameter: Target position — reachable vs unreachable changes behavior. Number of iterations vs convergence speed.
identities.triggers: Target in range → arm solves smoothly, target out of range → arm stretches toward (graceful degradation)
identities.emerges: Natural-looking arm motion from simple backward-forward passes. Joint angles from endpoint constraint.
identities.needs: VR grabbable target [missing — orbits automatically]. Segment count slider [missing]. Iteration count display [missing].
identities.relationships: Completes Joints_Kinematics. Contrasts with GimbalStabilizer (forward kinematics). Depends on chain concept from ChainSwing.
identities.truth: Specify where the hand should be. The math bends the arm. Animation becomes positioning endpoints.

identities.essence: A → -BF+AFA+FB-, B → +AF-BFB-FA+ in 3D with pitch/roll — a single path visits every point in a cube
identities.desire: To fill space with a single unbroken line — watch a path that never crosses itself touch every corner of a cube
identities.critical_parameter: generations — each increment multiplies path length by 8, from simple fold to space-saturating curve
identities.triggers: Generation 1 → simple bent path; generation 3 → dense space-filling weave; animated drawing → reveals the path order
identities.emerges: A continuous path through 3D space that preserves locality — nearby points on the path are nearby in space
identities.needs: VR generation controller [has], Label3D [has], animation toggle [has]
identities.relationships: Feeds into LSystems_Grammars_And_Curves. Pairs with space_filling_curve_gallery (3D vs 2D gallery).
identities.truth: A grammar can visit every point in space without crossing itself — infinity threaded through a cube.

identities.essence: X → F[+X]F[-X][^X][&X], F → FF at 90° with pitch/yaw branching — orthogonal L-system architecture
identities.desire: To generate a city from a seed — watch right-angle grammar produce buildings, bridges, and towers
identities.critical_parameter: iterations — complexity grows exponentially; each level adds branching in all six cardinal directions
identities.triggers: Iteration 2 → simple cross; iteration 4 → dense brutalist megastructure; slow rotation reveals 3D depth
identities.emerges: Building-like structures from botanical L-system rules reinterpreted with 90-degree angles
identities.needs: VR complexity controller [has], Label3D [has], auto-rotation [has]
identities.relationships: Feeds into LSystems_Architecture. Contrasts with lsystem_dungeon (3D growth vs 2D floor plan). Uses Turtle3D.
identities.truth: Change the angle from 25° to 90° and the tree becomes a city — architecture is botany with right angles.

identities.essence: if ray_cast(branch_tip, obstacle) → prune_branch(red_stub) else grow_forward
identities.desire: To grow around obstacles — a tree that senses its environment and adapts its shape accordingly
identities.critical_parameter: obstacle positions — the spatial constraints that force the tree to find alternative growth paths
identities.triggers: Obstacle near trunk → dramatic pruning, asymmetric crown; no obstacles → normal fractal plant
identities.emerges: Adaptive morphology from collision detection — the tree's shape encodes the obstacle layout
identities.needs: VR obstacle placement [missing], iteration control [missing], Label3D [has]
identities.relationships: Feeds into LSystems_Growth. Extends lsystem_tree (blind growth → environmentally aware). Uses physics raycasting.
identities.truth: Context sensitivity is how real trees grow — the environment is part of the grammar.

identities.essence: tree.dbh += nutrients * season * strategy * health; nutrients diffuse and deplete — competitive growth on shared soil
identities.desire: To grow a forest where trees compete — watch aggressive species starve neighbors, conservative ones endure winters
identities.critical_parameter: nutrient_supply vs competition_radius — together they determine whether the forest is cooperative or cutthroat
identities.triggers: Spring → growth burst; Winter → dormancy; aggressive strategy → fast growth but resource depletion; crown overlap → health decline
identities.emerges: Ecosystem dynamics from individual L-system trees sharing a diffusing nutrient grid — ecology from grammar
identities.needs: VR diffusion/nutrients/speed/trees controllers [has], Label3D [has], health graph [has]
identities.relationships: Central to LSystems_Competition. Extends lsystem_tree (single tree → competing forest). Uses allometric power laws.
identities.truth: Competition emerges when grammars share resources — ecology is grammar plus scarcity.

identities.essence: generation_timer → lsystem.generate() → interpret → draw_with_wind — growth made visible in time
identities.desire: To grow before your eyes — each generation adding branches with tapering thickness and wind sway
identities.critical_parameter: growth_delay — controls the pace of revelation, from instant to meditative
identities.triggers: Each generation adds depth, widens angles (angle_spread_per_gen), and adds leaves at terminal branches
identities.emerges: Wind animation on cached segments creates living motion — the tree breathes after it finishes growing
identities.needs: VR growth controls [missing], wind parameter sliders [missing], Label3D [has]
identities.relationships: Extends lsystem_tree (static → animated). Feeds into LSystems_Growth. Uses LSystem.create_fractal_plant().
identities.truth: Watching a tree grow generation by generation teaches more than seeing the final form.

identities.essence: w(i) *= exp(alpha * err_i). Points that the last stump got wrong get heavier. The next stump focuses on the hard cases.
identities.desire: Watch a sequence of weak learners (stumps) each specialize on what the previous one failed. The ensemble gets smarter by remembering its mistakes.
identities.critical_parameter: n_rounds — how many weak learners to add. Too few = underfitting. Too many = overfitting. The sweet spot is where the weighted vote stabilizes.
identities.triggers: Automatic — builds one stump per round, updates sample weights, shows accumulated decision boundary.
identities.emerges: Misclassified points grow visually larger as their weight increases. The ensemble boundary gets progressively more complex from simple stumps.
identities.needs: Auto-stepping simulation [has]. Missing: VR speed slider, pause/step controls.
identities.relationships: Contrasts with RandomForest (sequential vs parallel). Both are ensemble methods but with opposite strategies — boosting vs bagging.
identities.truth: AdaBoost is a conversation between failure and focus. Each mistake makes the next learner pay more attention to what was missed.

identities.essence: score(x) > threshold → anomaly; three heuristics: z-score, isolation radius, autoencoder error
identities.desire: see the boundary between normal and anomalous shift as you change methods and thresholds
identities.critical_parameter: threshold — determines where the decision boundary falls for each method
identities.triggers: cycling detection mode recolors all points; lowering threshold floods with false positives
identities.emerges: the realization that "anomaly" is not intrinsic — it depends entirely on which lens you use
identities.needs: VR controls for mode cycling [missing], threshold adjustment [missing] — exported params only
identities.relationships: contrasts enhanced_kmeans (clustering finds groups, anomaly detection finds outsiders); unlocks explainable_ai_xai_vr
identities.truth: anomaly is not a property of a point but a relationship between a point and the model judging it

identities.essence: output(x,y) = Σ kernel(i,j) · image(x+i, y+j) — convolution as local pattern matching
identities.desire: slide a kernel across an image with your hands, watch edges and features materialize
identities.critical_parameter: kernel weights — Sobel detects edges, Gaussian blurs, Sharpen enhances
identities.triggers: painting pixels changes the input image; applying different filters reveals different truths about the same data
identities.emerges: the realization that "seeing" is not passive — it requires a choice of what to look for
identities.needs: VR pixel painting [has conceptual], grabbable filter kernels [has], sliding kernel animation [has]
identities.relationships: unlocks convolutional_neural_networks_cnns_vr (learned kernels vs hand-designed); depends on neural_networks_vr (feature hierarchy)
identities.truth: every act of perception is a convolution — a commitment to which local patterns matter

identities.essence: feature_map = ReLU(input ⊛ kernel + bias); pool → repeat → dense → classify
identities.desire: walk through CNN layers as rooms, see feature maps shrink and deepen, feel hierarchy emerge
identities.critical_parameter: kernel_weights — each 3x3 grid decides what pattern a filter detects
identities.triggers: training_progress drives accuracy and activation pulsing; kernel editing changes learned features
identities.emerges: hierarchical feature extraction — edges → textures → parts → objects, without anyone prescribing it
identities.needs: grabbable kernel editors [has], feature map inspection [has], forward pass particle animation [has]
identities.relationships: depends on computer_vision_vr (hand-designed → learned kernels); contrasts neural_networks_vr (dense vs spatial connectivity)
identities.truth: the convolution is a bet that the same pattern can appear anywhere — translation invariance IS the inductive bias

identities.essence: fitness(creature) → tournament selection → crossover(genes₁, genes₂) → mutate → next generation
identities.desire: watch alien morphologies — symbiotic clusters, phase-shifting blobs, fractals — compete and evolve in VR
identities.critical_parameter: mutation_rate — governs the balance between exploitation (refining) and exploration (inventing)
identities.triggers: evolution_timer timeout breeds new generation; VR controller trigger raycasts to interact with creatures
identities.emerges: creature types nobody designed — symbiotic, phase-shifting, recursive, resonance, topology-changing
identities.needs: VR controller interaction [has], timer-based evolution [has]
identities.relationships: extends evolvingflowers (richer morphology space); contrasts 9_3_smart_rockets_vr (fixed body, optimized trajectory vs evolved body)
identities.truth: given enough variation and selection, form follows fitness without any designer

identities.essence: genome = {petals, color_hue, symmetry, L-system_rules, branch_angle}; fitness = symmetry + vibrancy + complexity
identities.desire: watch a garden of flowers evolve toward beauty — petals deepen in color, branching patterns elaborate
identities.critical_parameter: mutation_rate — shapes how quickly the aesthetic drifts; too high and beauty dissolves
identities.triggers: generation_time timer breeds new population; elite flowers survive; growth animation springs flowers up
identities.emerges: L-system branching patterns, color preferences, symmetry — an aesthetic nobody programmed
identities.needs: VR controls [missing] — generation_time and mutation_rate exported but no spatial sliders
identities.relationships: depends on 9_3_smart_rockets_vr (shared GA pattern); unlocks evolved_creatures (from flowers to creatures)
identities.truth: beauty is what survives selection — aesthetics can be an emergent property of optimization

identities.essence: explanation(model, input) → feature importance; three methods: SHAP (game theory), LIME (local surrogate), Grad-CAM (gradient attention)
identities.desire: see WHY a model decided — grab feature bars, walk through perturbation clouds, read attention heatmaps
identities.critical_parameter: feature_importance — the SHAP values that reveal which inputs the model actually used
identities.triggers: switching XAI methods recolors the entire scene; manipulating features changes the explanation
identities.emerges: the realization that different explanation methods disagree — there is no single "true" explanation
identities.needs: grabbable SHAP bars [has], perturbation cloud [has], heatmap visualization [has], counterfactual path [has]
identities.relationships: depends on neural_networks_vr (must have a model to explain); contrasts anomaly_detection (detecting vs explaining)
identities.truth: a model that cannot explain itself is not understood — it is merely obeyed

identities.essence: min_G max_D V(D,G) = E[log D(x)] + E[log(1 - D(G(z)))] — adversarial minimax game
identities.desire: stand between two competing neural networks, throw noise into the generator, judge fake vs real
identities.critical_parameter: competition_level — the balance between generator and discriminator drives quality
identities.triggers: training_progress drives both losses; generator_loss falling means fakes improving; competition pillar grows with quality
identities.emerges: Nash equilibrium where generated data becomes indistinguishable from real — creation from adversarial pressure
identities.needs: throwable noise particles [has], central competition arena [has], feedback loop particles [has]
identities.relationships: contrasts neural_networks_vr (discriminative vs generative); depends on gradient_descent_visualization (both networks optimize)
identities.truth: creation can emerge from opposition — the generator learns to create precisely because the discriminator learns to destroy

identities.essence: assign each point to nearest centroid; move centroids to cluster means; repeat until convergence
identities.desire: watch colored clusters crystallize from unlabeled chaos as centroids drift to their resting places
identities.critical_parameter: cluster_count (K) — choosing K is the fundamental unsupervised learning decision
identities.triggers: iteration step reassigns points and moves centroids; convergence stops when movement < threshold
identities.emerges: Voronoi tessellation of space; initialization sensitivity (K-means++ vs random); the elbow in the inertia curve
identities.needs: VR controls [missing] — has 2D UI buttons but no spatial VR sliders
identities.relationships: contrasts svm_visualization (supervised boundaries vs unsupervised clustering); unlocks random_forest_visualization (ensemble methods)
identities.truth: clustering does not discover structure in data — it imposes structure by choosing K

identities.essence: three landscapes from one dataset — the loss function is the author
identities.desire: players see that optimization answers depend on the question you formalize
identities.critical_parameter: outlier_fraction — how many data points are outliers
identities.triggers: instantiation, dataset perturbation slider
identities.emerges: the insight that loss functions are not discovered but designed
identities.needs: [implemented] 3 terrain meshes, gradient descent balls, Label3D equations, controls
identities.relationships: gradient_descent_landscape (single loss), optimization_algorithms (optimizer comparison)
identities.truth: the landscape is not given — it is authored

identities.essence: c(t) = f·c(t-1) + i·tanh(W·[h,x]); h(t) = o·tanh(c(t)) — three gates control memory flow
identities.desire: walk inside a room-scale LSTM cell, grab the forget/input/output gates, watch memory particles flow
identities.critical_parameter: forget_gate_activation — controls how much the cell remembers vs forgets at each step
