identities.essence: 50 particles orbiting a 3D fitness landscape, each pulled between their own best remembered position and the swarm's global best — trails trace the collective negotiation between individual memory and social pressure
identities.desire: to show that optimization is a political act — the diversity_preservation parameter is a literal resistance to premature convergence; the swarm that stays diverse finds more of the landscape
identities.critical_parameter: social_coefficient vs cognitive_coefficient balance (both 1.5 default) — high social pulls the swarm toward consensus, high cognitive keeps particles near their own history; together they define how collective the intelligence is
identities.triggers: each particle updates velocity using inertia + cognitive pull (toward personal best) + social pull (toward global best) + queer_resistance (mutation and diversity preservation); global_best updates whenever any particle finds a better fitness
identities.emerges: particles with high identity_fluidity resist the global best and continue exploring — they function as scouts; when a scout finds a new basin, the social coefficient pulls the rest of the swarm toward it
identities.needs: apply_grid_config [missing]; VR interaction to adjust inertia/social/cognitive live [missing]; objective function switching [has via export_enum]
identities.relationships: appears in SwarmIntelligence gallery alongside ant_colony artifacts; the queer_landscape objective function (option 4) explicitly models resistance to a single optimum; contrast with gradient_descent_landscape (deterministic, single path)
identities.truth: a swarm that never converges finds more — diversity_preservation is not inefficiency but epistemological humility about whether you have found the right answer or just an answer

identities.essence: v_i(t+1) = ω·v_i(t) + c1·r1·(pbest_i - x_i) + c2·r2·(gbest - x_i) — velocity is nostalgia plus social pressure plus momentum
identities.desire: to watch particles swarm a multi-peaked landscape and see them settle into the global maximum without any single particle understanding what "global" means

identities.triggers: when the landscape's central peak is globally best, all particles eventually abandon personal bests to converge on the center — a visible collective capitulation
identities.emerges: temporary sub-swarms that cluster around local peaks before the global best signal pulls them away — visible competition between exploitation and exploration

identities.truth: remembering where you were best is not enough — you also need to know where the group was best; all optimization is a negotiation between self and collective

identities.relationships: used in vectors sequence; the gyroscope gadget adds interactive orientation feedback
identities.truth: a coordinate system is a choice of three mutually perpendicular directions with an agreed origin

identities.essence: v = |v| * v-hat. A vector is magnitude times direction. Decompose into (x,y,z) components.
identities.desire: To grab an arrow and stretch it — watching magnitude, unit vector, and components all update as one system.
identities.critical_parameter: The dragged endpoint of vector_a. Its position simultaneously defines magnitude, direction, and all three components.
identities.triggers: Drag endpoint → magnitude arc sweeps, unit vector rescales, component arrows resize along axes, spring gadget deflects
identities.emerges: The magnitude arc dotting from the x-axis toward the vector tip. The spring scale responding to vector length like a physical instrument.
identities.needs: Grabbable vector endpoint [has], component decomposition [has], spring scale gadget [has]. Missing: VR button to toggle component visibility.
identities.relationships: Entry point for all vector artifacts. Foundation for basis_vectors_rig (decomposition) and dot_product_projector (magnitude in dot product formula).
identities.truth: A vector is not a number and not a point. It is a displacement — a difference between two positions, carrying both how far and which way.

identities.essence: (a + b)[i] = a[i] + b[i] — add each component; geometrically: place b's tail at a's tip, the result reaches from origin to b's new tip
identities.desire: to make the parallelogram visible — the two vectors from origin, the sum along the diagonal, the invisible shape that proves tip-to-tail and component addition are the same thing
identities.critical_parameter: piston_gadget — dragging either vector updates the sum in real time, making addition tactile rather than symbolic
identities.triggers: VectorWorkbench spawns scene → vectors initialized → _process updates sum_vector each frame as a.target + b.target
identities.emerges: the parallelogram — dotted lines project a and b's paths, framing the sum vector as their shared diagonal
identities.needs: VR grab to drag vector tips [missing], component readout labels [has], real-time sum update [has]
identities.relationships: prerequisite to VectorSubtraction (subtraction is addition of negative); foundational to VectorForces where vectors combine as physical forces
identities.truth: Vector addition is not about arrows — it is about the fact that two displacements taken sequentially are equivalent to one displacement.

identities.essence: a·b = |a||b|cos(θ) = a.x*b.x + a.y*b.y + a.z*b.z — a scalar measuring how much two vectors agree in direction
identities.desire: to make alignment visible — the projection vector shows exactly how much of a lands on b, and the hinge_gadget makes the angle between them physical
identities.critical_parameter: angle θ — at 0° the dot product equals |a||b| (full agreement), at 90° it is zero (pure perpendicularity), at 180° it is negative (opposition)
identities.triggers: hinge_gadget tilts vector_b → angle between a and b changes → projection_vector = (a·b/|b|²)*b recomputed each frame → rejection_vector = a - projection
identities.emerges: projection and rejection — the dot product splits a into two components: one along b (the agreement) and one perpendicular to b (the independence)
identities.needs: VR grab to explore angle space [missing], hinge panel interaction [has], projection length readout [has]
identities.relationships: prerequisite to VectorCrossProduct (cross uses sin, dot uses cos, together they measure all of angle); used in VectorForces to project forces onto axes
identities.truth: The dot product does not measure length — it measures how much two directions agree. At 90°, they are strangers.

identities.essence: a - b = a + (-b) — flip b to its negative, then add; difference_vector points from b's tip to a's tip
identities.desire: to show that subtraction is relabeled addition — -b is b reversed, and the balance_beam gadget makes the equivalence felt rather than memorized
identities.critical_parameter: negative_b — the negated vector rendered in parallel shows why a-b ≠ b-a; switching which is negated flips the direction of the result
identities.triggers: VectorWorkbench spawns → negative_b = -b computed → difference_vector = a + negative_b → tip_tail_neg_b positions negative_b at a's tip
identities.emerges: the direction between two tips — a-b always points from b's tip to a's tip, making it the vector "from B to A" and giving subtraction spatial meaning
identities.needs: VR grab to drag vector tips [missing], balance beam interaction [has via balance_gadget]
identities.relationships: inverse of VectorAddition; reveals dot product geometry (a-b magnitude appears in the law of cosines)
identities.truth: Subtraction is directional memory — a-b is the vector that, if you followed b, would tell you where a is.

identities.essence: F_net = gravity + thrust + drag; drag = -DRAG_COEFFICIENT * velocity; a = F_net / mass; velocity integrates acceleration each frame
identities.desire: to see Newton's second law in real time — gravity pulls, thrust fights back, drag resists motion, and the ball trajectory shows what the sum decides
identities.critical_parameter: DRAG_COEFFICIENT (0.8) — too high and the ball stops immediately; zero and it goes parabolic; the visible drag arrow shows the invisible resistance
identities.triggers: catapult_gadget launches ball → each frame: compute gravity/thrust/drag vectors → sum to F_net → update RigidBody3D → render all 6 vectors simultaneously
identities.emerges: the visible taxonomy of forces — five simultaneous arrows (gravity, thrust, drag, velocity, acceleration) let you watch how each contributes before they combine
identities.needs: VR catapult launch [has via catapult_gadget], thrust magnitude control [missing], drag coefficient slider [missing]
identities.relationships: the applied combination of VectorAddition (force superposition) and VectorDotProduct (drag opposes velocity direction); prerequisite to VectorTorque
identities.truth: A force is a direction with a claim. When two forces disagree, the net force is the argument they settle at.

identities.essence: a×b = [a.y*b.z - a.z*b.y, a.z*b.x - a.x*b.z, a.x*b.y - a.y*b.x] — a vector perpendicular to both, magnitude |a||b|sin(θ), direction by right-hand rule
identities.desire: to feel rotation emerge from two directions — the cross product lives in the axis of the rotation that would carry a into b, and the paddle_wheel makes this visceral
identities.critical_parameter: the right-hand rule — cross product is anti-commutative (a×b = -(b×a)), and the paddle wheel visualizes this as clockwise vs counterclockwise spin
identities.triggers: vector_a and vector_b positions → cross_vector = a.cross(b) computed each frame → parallelogram mesh spans both vectors → paddle_gadget spins proportional to magnitude
identities.emerges: the parallelogram area — |a×b| is exactly the area of the parallelogram formed by a and b, making the cross product a measurement of 2D span embedded in 3D
identities.needs: VR grab to explore plane configurations [missing], paddle wheel interaction [has], parallelogram area display [has]
identities.relationships: complement to VectorDotProduct (dot=cos, cross=sin, both needed for full angle); used in VectorTorque where torque = radius × force
identities.truth: The cross product does not live in the plane of its inputs — it lives perpendicular to it, measuring how much rotation is implied by two directions.

identities.essence: impact → destroy(method). Eight destruction methods: instant, health-based, face-peel, Cantor recursion, Voronoi fracture, planar crack, prism shatter. Topology of breaking.
identities.desire: To throw balls at things and watch them break differently — each destructible teaching a different algorithm for decomposing geometry under impact.
identities.critical_parameter: The velocity of the thrown ball at impact. It triggers destruction thresholds and determines fragment ejection speeds. Faster throw = more dramatic break.
identities.triggers: VR grab + throw → ball hits destructible, each type responds differently (instant/health/recursive-split/voronoi-crack/prism-shatter), stats track throws and destroys
identities.emerges: Cantor boxes splitting into 4, then each quarter splitting again (recursive fractal destruction). Voronoi spheres cracking along Voronoi cell boundaries. Each method feels different.
identities.needs: Throwable balls [has], 8 destructible types [has], info panel [has]. Missing: VR reset button, slow-motion replay of destruction.
identities.relationships: Sandbox for all destruction algorithms in the throwing system. Lives in ForcesArena. Tests subsystems used by VectorThrowing targets.
identities.truth: Destruction is topology change. How something breaks reveals how it was built.

identities.essence: sphere → fragments(method). Five fracture algorithms: planar cut, octree division, orange-peel sectors, CSG boolean, pre-segmented mesh. One sphere, five deaths.
identities.desire: To compare how the same sphere breaks under five different mathematical decompositions — each one a different answer to "how do you divide a sphere?"
identities.critical_parameter: The impact point and velocity of the thrown ball. For planar cuts, the impact plane determines the split. For Voronoi, the crack propagates from impact. Geometry meets ballistics.
identities.triggers: VR grab + throw → ball hits sphere, each sphere type fractures by its algorithm, stats track throws and total splits, per-sphere piece counts update live
identities.emerges: Planar cuts producing clean halves. Octree producing eight cubic chunks. Sectors peeling like an orange. CSG producing irregular but realistic cuts. Each algorithm's personality visible in its fragments.
identities.needs: Throwable balls [has], five sphere types [has], per-sphere info labels [has], live piece counters [has]. Missing: slow-motion mode, side-by-side comparison replay.
identities.relationships: Companion to destructibles_test_scene (cubes + planes vs spheres). Lives in ForcesArena. Showcases computational geometry algorithms through destruction.
identities.truth: There is no single way to break a sphere. Each fracture method is a decomposition basis — a different answer to what "parts" means.

identities.essence: p(t) = p0 + v0*t + 0.5*g*t^2. Projectile motion. Horizontal = constant velocity; vertical = constant acceleration. Your hand writes the initial conditions.
identities.desire: To throw. To feel velocity leave your hand, watch gravity bend the arc, and hit something that shatters. Physics as sport.
identities.critical_parameter: The release velocity from your VR hand. Direction and magnitude together determine the entire trajectory — the parabola is written at release.
identities.triggers: VR grab + release → ball launches with hand velocity, trajectory line predicts path, target hit → score + signal, drone destroyed → points + respawn timer
identities.emerges: Accuracy improving as the learner internalizes the parabola. Leading the drone target. The trajectory preview teaching prediction before the throw.
identities.needs: VR throwable balls [has], target grid [has], homing drone [has], trajectory preview [has], score display [has]. Missing: wind force perturbation.
identities.relationships: Culmination of VectorAdvanced. Uses projectile physics from ForceMagnitudeDemo. Drone uses subtraction/normalization from hl_turret_vectors (but as enemy AI).
identities.truth: A throw is an initial condition. After release, you have no control. Physics decides the rest.

identities.essence: desired = (target - position).normalized() * speed. Chase, prepare, shoot, cooldown. A state machine driven by vector subtraction.
identities.desire: To hunt. To orbit at ideal_distance, charge projectiles, fire in bursts, and kamikaze when dying — an adversary that teaches vectors by trying to kill you.
identities.critical_parameter: ideal_distance (4.0 units) — the range the drone wants to maintain. Too close = backs up. Too far = approaches. In range = switches to attack states.
identities.triggers: Player position → chase/orbit, prepare timer → spawn held projectiles, shoot timer → fire burst, health reaches 0 → kamikaze mode (speed boost, explosion, damage)
identities.emerges: The drone's strafing pattern from sinusoidal offsets. Leading shots via look_at. Kamikaze desperation creating final-moment tension.
identities.needs: State machine AI [has], burst-fire system [has], kamikaze mode [has], VR player tracking [has]. Missing: difficulty scaling, formation flying with multiple drones.
identities.relationships: Enemy counterpart to hl_turret_vectors (player-controlled targeting vs AI targeting). Sub-component of VectorThrowing. Uses subtraction and normalization as core AI.
identities.truth: The drone is a mirror of the turret. Same math, opposite role. Subtraction works for both hunter and hunted.

identities.essence: An arrangement of shootable spheres — grid, circle, or pyramid — providing physics targets for the gravity gun
identities.desire: To give the player something to push, throw, knock — to make the abstract gravity gun palpable through impact and rearrangement
identities.critical_parameter: spawn_pattern and spawn_count — pattern decides whether the arrangement reads as wall, ring, or stack; count decides intensity
identities.triggers: Grid pattern produces brick wall feel; circle gives ring-toss-like target; pyramid stacks for cascade physics
identities.emerges: A simple arrangement of physics objects becomes a stage for vector practice — every shot is a vector being applied at a point
identities.needs: configurable spawn patterns [has], physics-active spheres [has], reset on map enter [has]
identities.relationships: Stage for gravity_gun in forces/Combat_Arena. Companion to queer_cylinder_target (the named goal among the spheres)
identities.truth: A test scene is not a placeholder — it is the rehearsal where physics learns its part before the player arrives.

identities.essence: τ = r × F; |τ| = |r||F|sin(θ); moment arm r_perp = r - (r·F̂)F̂; torque is the rotational force around a pivot, magnitude proportional to the moment arm length
identities.desire: to feel why a long wrench works better — radius_vector and force_vector combine via cross product to show how distance from pivot multiplies the turning power
identities.critical_parameter: the angle between r and F — at 90° torque is maximum (force fully perpendicular to lever arm); at 0° it is zero (pushing along the arm does nothing)
identities.triggers: radius_vector and force_vector spawned → _process: torque_vector = r.cross(F) → moment_arm = r - r.project(F̂) → all three rendered with live readout
identities.emerges: the moment arm r_perp — visible as the green vector, it is the part of r that is perpendicular to F, and its length is what actually determines the torque magnitude
identities.needs: VR pivot grab [missing], interactive radius drag [has via GrabSphere], force direction control [missing]
identities.relationships: applies VectorCrossProduct to physics; the rotational equivalent of VectorForces (linear); appears in the forces sequence after understanding basic force composition
identities.truth: Torque is leverage made mathematical — the cross product measures how much of your force is wasted pushing toward the pivot, and gives you only the turning remainder.

identities.essence: F(p) = swirl(p) - radial(p). A vector field assigns a direction to every point. The particle reads the field and follows.
identities.desire: To make an invisible flow visible — 81 arrows breathing in unison, a particle tracing the field's will.
identities.critical_parameter: The swirl-to-radial ratio in _field_value(). It determines whether the field spirals inward, orbits, or ejects.
identities.triggers: Automatic — arrows oscillate vertically, particle advects continuously. R → reset particle to origin, Space → freeze velocity.
identities.emerges: Spiral trajectories from the combination of rotational swirl and inward radial pull. The particle's path is never a straight line.
identities.needs: MultiMesh arrows [has], particle tracer [has]. Missing: VR slider to blend swirl vs radial, grabbable field source.
identities.relationships: Applied version of force_field_visualizer (same concept, different rendering). Feeds into weather_vector_field (wind as vector field).
identities.truth: A vector field is a set of instructions written in space. The particle has no memory and no plan — it only reads the local instruction.

identities.essence: p += v; v += g; if(wall) v *= -e. Position accumulates velocity, velocity accumulates gravity, walls reverse and damp.
identities.desire: To trap motion in a box and watch it slowly die — each bounce lower than the last, energy leaking into the walls.
identities.critical_parameter: _elasticity (0.9) — the fraction of speed kept per bounce. At 1.0 the ball bounces forever; below 1.0 it decays exponentially.
identities.triggers: Automatic — ball launches with initial velocity, gravity pulls down every frame, boundary collision reverses and damps per-axis
identities.emerges: The parabolic arc between bounces. The trail drawing the ball’s history as a fading line. The slow settling as elasticity drains energy.
identities.needs: Auto-running simulation [has], trail visualization [has]. Missing: VR grab to relaunch, elasticity slider, gravity toggle.
identities.relationships: Simplest dynamics artifact in forces. Foundation for exercise_1_8 (adds attraction). Contrasts with momentum_collision (two bodies vs one).
identities.truth: A bouncing ball is a clock that runs down. Each bounce measures how much the universe forgot.

identities.essence: steer = (desired - velocity).clamp(max_force). Seek + arrival. Distance to target scales desired speed.
identities.desire: to watch a ball chase a moving target, accelerating when far and decelerating when close — smooth arrival from pure math
identities.critical_parameter: max_force — the steering budget. High force = snappy turns. Low force = lazy curves. The tightness of the feedback loop.
identities.triggers: automatic — target traces sinusoidal curves, ball steers toward it every frame
identities.emerges: smooth deceleration zone near the target where speed ramps down proportionally to distance
identities.needs: auto-running simulation [has]. Missing: VR grabbable target, max_force slider, trail visualization
identities.relationships: extends bouncing_ball (adds steering instead of bouncing). Prepares for boid_flocking (many agents steering). Contrasts with exercise_1_8 (attraction vs steering).
identities.truth: smooth arrival is not a decision — it is a feedback loop. The closer you get, the gentler the approach.

identities.essence: F = strength * dir / r^2. Inverse-square attraction. Closer = stronger. Orbit emerges from falling and missing.
identities.desire: To let the learner grab the attractor in VR and drag it — watching the orbiting ball reshape its path in real time.
identities.critical_parameter: attraction_strength — controls the force constant. Too weak → ball escapes. Too strong → ball spirals inward. The sweet spot produces stable orbits.
identities.triggers: VR grab attractor sphere → ball orbit changes shape, strength slider → orbits tighten or loosen, velocity clamped at 0.15 to prevent escape
identities.emerges: Elliptical orbits from the interplay of tangential velocity and radial attraction. Moving the attractor mid-orbit creates chaotic transitions between orbit shapes.
identities.needs: VR grabbable attractor [has], strength parameter controller [has], force line visualization [has]. Missing: trail showing orbit history.
identities.relationships: Extends bouncing_ball (adds attraction). Feeds into three_body_problem and nbody_simulation (many attractors). Gateway to gravitational dynamics.
identities.truth: An orbit is a perpetual fall that always misses the ground. Attraction creates structure from nothing but distance and direction.

identities.essence: two grab-spheres with a line drawn between them — the most concrete vector you can hold
identities.desire: feel that a vector IS the relation between two points — move either endpoint and the magnitude updates live
identities.critical_parameter: grab-sphere positions — the entire vector is determined by where the two points sit
identities.triggers: _ready() wires the dropped signals; _process() refreshes geometry every frame from current endpoint positions
identities.emerges: a live line + arrow tip + length label that you can stretch, rotate, and reposition by grabbing
identities.needs: grab-sphere endpoint controllers [present]; length label [present]; arrow tip visualization [present]
identities.relationships: line primitive companion to point primitive; foundation for line_builder_3d (chain of vectors) and vectors-chapter examples
identities.truth: A vector is not a thing, it is a relation. Naming "from" and "to" produces it; moving either redraws everything that depends on it.

identities.essence: r = v - 2(v·n)n — the mirror law as pure linear algebra
identities.desire: rotate the surface, swing the incoming ray, watch the reflection obey the formula
identities.critical_parameter: surface_angle and vector_angle sliders — together they set the geometry
identities.triggers: slider_moved on either slider recalculates the entire reflection diagram
identities.emerges: equal angles of incidence and reflection — a consequence of the dot product
identities.needs: RackTemplates panel with two sliders [has]; Label3D formula display [has]
identities.relationships: builds on dot_product; feeds ray_tracing, billiard simulations, optics
identities.truth: Reflection is the simplest thing a vector can do to a surface — and it explains mirrors, echoes, and billiards.

identities.essence: a universal vector workbench — two draggable 3D vectors with live computed outputs for addition, subtraction, dot product, cross product, and projection
identities.desire: to make linear algebra touchable — the player grabs Vector A and Vector B in VR, moves them through space, and watches the dot product change as the angle between them changes; the formula is not read, it is felt
identities.critical_parameter: current_mode (Mode enum) — switches the display to highlight one operation at a time; ALL shows every result vector simultaneously, focused modes hide the others so the learner sees one relationship clearly
identities.triggers: _ready() spawns two draggable vectors + four result vectors + sliders + buttons; _process() reads current vector positions every frame and updates all five operations; slider_moved signals drive VR input path
identities.emerges: the parallelogram — when cross product mode is active, a filled parallelogram appears between A and B showing the magnitude of A×B as an area; the geometric interpretation of the cross product becomes visible space
identities.needs: apply_grid_config [has — stub]; VR slider controls [has — 6 component sliders]; mode buttons [has — 5 mode buttons]; keyboard mode switching [has — keys 1-5]; grab interaction [has via vector_scene_base]
identities.relationships: vectors sequence companion to vector_magnitude_demo; extends vector_scene_base (shared spawning, axes, floor); placed in Vectors_Intro map
identities.truth: a vector is not a number — it is a direction with commitment; VectorWorkbench proves this by making the commitment graspable and showing what two directions do to each other

identities.essence: f_beat = |f_a - f_b| — difference becomes rhythm
identities.desire: drag two frequencies close together and hear/see the slow pulse emerge from their interference
identities.critical_parameter: freq_a and freq_b sliders — the smaller the gap, the slower the beat
identities.triggers: slider_moved on either frequency recalculates the wave animation
identities.emerges: the beat envelope — a slow amplitude modulation born from two fast oscillations
identities.needs: RackTemplates panel with two sliders [has]; 3 rows of spheres [has]; Label3D [has]
identities.relationships: builds on sine_oscillation; connects to fourier_transform, standing_waves, resonance
identities.truth: When two nearly identical things interfere, their tiny difference becomes the loudest signal.

identities.essence: column(h) = r * (cos(spiral_density*h), h, sin(spiral_density*h)) with sine/cosine amplitude modulation
identities.desire: Stand among baroque spiral columns that twist with trigonometric functions and emit organ tones
identities.critical_parameter: spiral_density — controls how many helical turns per column height
identities.triggers: time animates subtle column rotation; audio_phase drives organ sound generation
identities.emerges: the baroque as frozen oscillation — architecture that remembers the wave that shaped it
identities.needs: VR walkthrough [has], audio playback [has]
identities.relationships: depends on procedural spiral mesh generation; contrasts with sine_cylinder_staircase (decorative vs functional spirals); unlocks wave-as-architecture
identities.truth: A spiral column is a sine wave wrapped around a vertical axis.

identities.essence: a turtle-graphics pipe network grown from string commands — `f` adds anchors, `r`/`l` bend bezier handles, `t`/`x` branch into independent curves; SurfaceTool extrudes one continuous mesh along the path
identities.desire: to make pipe-as-composition feel like writing a sentence — type "f r f l f" and the system turns where you said it would; the pipe IS the score
identities.critical_parameter: config_file or turtle command string — every junction, elbow, and branch lives in the string; geometry is just rendered grammar
identities.triggers: _ready() runs the auto_build pass; build_pipe_system() walks turtle commands, sets bezier IN/OUT handles per anchor, extrudes circular cross-sections via sample_baked tangent frames
identities.emerges: cathedral-organ topology from text — branching drain networks the player can walk through, with smooth corners that cost two lines of bezier instead of a hundred lines of arc math
identities.needs: VR walking inside pipes [has]; per-segment audio routing [missing]; runtime turtle editing [missing]; apply_grid_config [missing]
identities.relationships: pairs with seismograph (the readout) and coupled_oscillator_lattice (the medium) to form the wavefunctions plumbing-as-resonance arc; appears in Gravity Creates Rhythm, Sound as Waveform, Spatial Sound Laboratory
identities.truth: a pipe is a path with mass — when you bend a command string, you bend the air column, and the geometry becomes the instrument

identities.essence: r(u,v) = waist + (hem-waist)*u, modulated by sin(v*TAU + wave*u)
identities.desire: Watch fabric ripple as sine waves propagate through a procedural dress mesh
identities.critical_parameter: wave_intensity — transforms static garment into living oscillation
identities.triggers: set_wave_intensity() deforms the parametric surface in real-time
identities.emerges: cloth-like motion from pure trigonometric displacement of vertices
identities.needs: VR sliders for wave parameters [missing], skeleton attachment [has]
identities.relationships: depends on SurfaceTool mesh generation; contrasts with ruth_asawa_sculpture (fabric vs wire); unlocks wearable wave visualization
identities.truth: Fabric is a surface that remembers every wave that passes through it.

identities.essence: X(f) = sum(x(t) * e^(-2*pi*i*f*t)) — decomposes a composite waveform into frequency spectrum bars; 5 harmonics + noise synthesized in time domain, DFT computed per frame for visualization
identities.desire: to see a messy waveform dissolve into clean frequency bars — to hear the sci-fi theremin audio that the same harmonics produce while watching them separate visually
identities.critical_parameter: fundamental_freq — the base frequency whose integer multiples (harmonics) compose the signal; changing it shifts the entire spectrum
identities.triggers: _process updates waveform in real time, computes simplified DFT, animates transform engine and data flow particles; AudioStreamGenerator produces theremin-like audio from the same harmonics
identities.emerges: the data flow particles tracing sinusoidal paths between time and frequency domains make the abstract transform physically visible — information flows through the machine
identities.needs: [missing] no VR slider_horizontal or push_button — no interactive control of fundamental_freq or noise_level; relies on .tscn scene tree nodes ($TimeDomain, $FrequencyDomain, etc.)
identities.relationships: the core artifact for F17_Zen_Garden (contemplative mathematical object); connects to spectrum_display (frequency analysis) and standing_waves (wave physics)
identities.truth: every signal is a sum of pure frequencies — the Fourier transform does not create this decomposition, it reveals the one that was always there

identities.essence: sculpture(t) = core + petals(sin(morph*t)) + tendrils(sin(pulse*t)) + orbital_rings
identities.desire: Witness a Kusama-inspired sculpture pulse, morph, and shift color in obsessive oscillation
identities.critical_parameter: detail_scale — controls geometric complexity of petals, tendrils, and orbital elements
identities.triggers: time drives morph_time, pulse_time, and color_time through layered sine animations
identities.emerges: obsessive visual density — polka dots as high-frequency oscillation of attention
identities.needs: VR spatial presence [has], detail/color controls [missing]
identities.relationships: depends on multi-layered procedural mesh generation; contrasts with ruth_asawa_sculpture (Kusama excess vs Asawa restraint); unlocks art-as-oscillation
identities.truth: Obsessive repetition is oscillation at maximum frequency — the dot is the shortest wavelength of attention.

identities.essence: catenary(x) approximated by cubic spline through grabbable control points
identities.desire: Grab control points in VR and sculpt hanging cable curves in real-time
identities.critical_parameter: control_point_count — determines degrees of freedom for curve shaping
identities.triggers: moving any control point recomputes the spline and regenerates the cable mesh
identities.emerges: natural catenary sag from gravity acting on flexible curves between fixed points
identities.needs: VR grab on control points [has], cable thickness control [missing]
identities.relationships: depends on Curve3D spline interpolation; contrasts with BigPipeSystem (flexible vs rigid segments); unlocks curve intuition
identities.truth: A hanging cable finds the shape that minimizes potential energy — nature solves calculus of variations.

identities.essence: N points connected into a polyline — drag any point and the whole line redraws
identities.desire: see the line as a chain of vector relations, each one independently editable
identities.critical_parameter: point_count and point_spacing — they set the chain's length and initial geometry
identities.triggers: _ready() spawns the points; _process() rebuilds the mesh whenever points have moved
identities.emerges: a continuous polyline whose shape is the live consequence of every point's position
identities.needs: point_scene injection [present]; point count slider [missing]; per-point grab handle [present via point_scene]
identities.relationships: extends vectorline (two-point case) to N points; foundation for spline_curve / Bezier / polyline-based wave samplers in wavefunctions
identities.truth: A polyline is the simplest function-of-index. By making the indices grabbable, the function becomes editable — geometry as direct manipulation.

identities.essence: (x,y,z) = (A_x*sin(a*t+delta), A_y*sin(b*t), A_z*sin(c*t)) — parametric Lissajous
identities.desire: Watch a glowing particle trace beautiful closed curves defined by frequency ratios
identities.critical_parameter: freq_ratio_x / freq_ratio_y — rational ratios close the curve, irrational ratios fill space
identities.triggers: time drives the parametric position; preset selection switches between classic ratio combinations
identities.emerges: complex geometric figures from the interference of perpendicular oscillations
identities.needs: VR frequency ratio control [missing], 3D rotation [has]
identities.relationships: depends on ImmediateMesh trail rendering; contrasts with SphericalHarmonics (planar vs spherical oscillation); unlocks frequency ratio visualization
identities.truth: The ratio of two frequencies determines whether a curve closes or wanders forever.

identities.essence: FM synthesis — carrier(t) * sin(mod_ratio * carrier * mod_index)
identities.desire: Grab two balls in VR to sculpt sound through frequency modulation
identities.critical_parameter: mod_index — controls harmonic richness from pure tone to metallic chaos
identities.triggers: ball position changes map to carrier freq, attack, decay, mod ratio, mod index, mod decay
identities.emerges: bell tones, electric pianos, brass — all from one oscillator modulating another
identities.needs: VR grab for both balls [has], preset buttons [has]
identities.relationships: depends on AudioStreamPlayer3D; contrasts with MarioSoundController (FM vs basic waveforms); unlocks timbre_sculptor
